source_body_en: PURPOSE: Accurate prediction of locoregional recurrence (LRR) in oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) is needed to guide treatment de-escalation decisions, but validated prognostic models integrating imaging and clinical data are lacking. We developed and evaluated a multimodal deep learning model combining pretreatment computed tomography (CT) with clinical variables to predict LRR. METHODS: In this retrospective multicenter prognostic study, we assembled 1,384 patients with histologically confirmed OPSCC treated with definitive radiotherapy with or without concurrent chemotherapy and without surgical resection of the primary tumor. Data were drawn from 1 private institutional archive and five publicly available archives. A cross-attention model fusing CT and clinical features was compared with feature concatenation, clinical-only, and imaging-only models. The primary outcome was LRR. Discrimination was assessed by Harrell Concordance Index (C-index) across 3-fold cross-validation, and risk stratification by Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank testing. Attribution analysis was used to identify influential predictors. RESULTS: LRR occurred in 161 of 1,384 patients (11.6%) over a median follow-up of 59.8 months (interquartile range, 25.8-89.0 months). The cross-attention model achieved the highest mean C-index, 0.718 (range, 0.699-0.734), followed by the clinical-only (0.705; range, 0.680-0.735), feature concatenation (0.697; range, 0.673-0.721), and imaging-only (0.674; range, 0.666-0.680) models. High-risk patients had significantly shorter LRR-free survival than low-risk patients in all three folds (log-rank P < .001 for each). Smoking history and human papillomavirus status were the most influential clinical predictors. CONCLUSION: A multimodal cross-attention deep learning model integrating CT with clinical variables showed numerically better discrimination for LRR prediction in OPSCC than unimodal approaches. Prospective external validation is required before such models inform individualized treatment decisions.
abstract_zh: 目的:需要准确预测口咽鳞状细胞癌(OPSCC)的局部区域复发(LRR)来指导 治疗 降级决策,但缺乏整合影像和临床数据的经过验证的预后模型。我们开发并评估了一种多模式深度学习模型,将治疗前计算机断层扫描 (CT) 与临床变量相结合来预测 LRR。方法:在这项回顾性多中心预后研究中,我们收集了 1,384 名经组织学证实的 OPSCC 患者,接受根治性放疗,联合或不联合化疗,且未手术切除原发肿瘤。数据取自 1 个私人机构档案馆和 5 个公开档案馆。将融合 CT 和临床特征的交叉注意力模型与特征串联、仅临床和仅成像模型进行比较。主要结局是LRR。通过 3 倍交叉验证的 Harrell 一致性指数(C 指数)评估歧视,并通过 Kaplan-Meier 分析和对数秩检验进行风险分层。归因分析用于识别有影响力的预测因素。结果:在中位随访时间 59.8 个月(四分位数范围,25.8-89.0 个月)内,1,384 名患者中有 161 名 (11.6%) 发生 LRR。交叉注意力模型实现了最高的平均 C 指数,0.718(范围,0.699-0.734),其次是仅临床模型(0.705;范围,0.680-0.735)、特征串联模型(0.697;范围,0.673-0.721)和仅成像模型(0.674;范围,0.666-0.680)型号。在所有三个方面,高风险患者的无 LRR 生存期均显着短于低风险患者(每个对数秩 P < .001)。吸烟史和 人乳头瘤病毒 状态是最有影响力的临床预测因素。结论:将 CT 与临床变量相结合的多模态交叉注意力深度学习模型在 OPSCC 中的 LRR 预测方面显示出比单模态方法更好的数值辨别力。在此类模型告知个性化 治疗 决策之前,需要进行前瞻性外部验证。

title: Differences in HPV-related gynaecological malignancies incidence and survival by individual and contextual variables: a population-based study
abstract: Abstract Vulvar, vaginal and cervical cancers are gynaecological malignancies that share a key risk factor: infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). As an HPV vaccine is available, many tumours are considered preventable. This study analysed the incidence and survival of vulvar, vaginal and cervical cancers in women living in the Community of Madrid (CM) from 2018–2020, by socioeconomic status and stage. Data of invasive tumours were extracted from the Population-Based Cancer Registry of Madrid (PBCR-CM). Descriptive analyses were performed for sociodemographic and tumour characteristics. Crude, age-specific and age-standardised incidence rates were calculated. Five-year observed and net survival were calculated, globally and stratified by socioeconomic status and stage. Flexible parametric models were adjusted to determine differences in the risk of death by stage. Between 2018–2020, 954 patients were diagnosed, corresponding to an age-standardised rate of 10.8 cases per 100 000 women-years. Most tumours are squamous cell carcinomas, grade II, and diagnosed at early stages. Cervical cancer patients showed greater survival results (71% vs 50% for vulvar/vaginal cancer). Survival was lowest among patients with grade-III and metastatic tumours. This study provides an overview of HPV-related gynaecological cancers in CM. To address inequalities, PBCR plays an indispensable role by ensuring high-quality epidemiological surveillance.

title_zh: HPV 相关妇科恶性肿瘤 发病率 和生存率的个体和环境变量差异:一项基于人群的研究
source_body_en: Abstract Vulvar, vaginal and cervical cancers are gynaecological malignancies that share a key risk factor: infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV). As an HPV vaccine is available, many tumours are considered preventable. This study analysed the incidence and survival of vulvar, vaginal and cervical cancers in women living in the Community of Madrid (CM) from 2018–2020, by socioeconomic status and stage. Data of invasive tumours were extracted from the Population-Based Cancer Registry of Madrid (PBCR-CM). Descriptive analyses were performed for sociodemographic and tumour characteristics. Crude, age-specific and age-standardised incidence rates were calculated. Five-year observed and net survival were calculated, globally and stratified by socioeconomic status and stage. Flexible parametric models were adjusted to determine differences in the risk of death by stage. Between 2018–2020, 954 patients were diagnosed, corresponding to an age-standardised rate of 10.8 cases per 100 000 women-years. Most tumours are squamous cell carcinomas, grade II, and diagnosed at early stages. Cervical cancer patients showed greater survival results (71% vs 50% for vulvar/vaginal cancer). Survival was lowest among patients with grade-III and metastatic tumours. This study provides an overview of HPV-related gynaecological cancers in CM. To address inequalities, PBCR plays an indispensable role by ensuring high-quality epidemiological surveillance.

title: HPV-driven DNA methylation plasticity reshapes immune regulation in head and neck cancer
abstract: Abstract The incidence of HPV-related HNC has exponentially increased over recent decades in head and neck cancer (HNC). Although HPV infection is known to reprogram the host epigenetic landscape, the cellular and functional consequences of HPV-mediated DNA methylation changes remain poorly defined. Here we demonstrated that HPV-driven epigenetic reprogramming reshapes immune regulation within the HNC tumor microenvironment (TME), generating distinct methylation landscapes associated with viral status. Genome-wide methylation analysis identified differentially methylated loci enriched in immune-related pathways, supporting a central role for epigenetic remodeling in shaping HPV-specific tumor–immune interactions. To link epigenetic differences to cellular organization and function within the TME, we characterized immune and stromal compartments, cell–cell interactions, and spatial architecture using high-dimensional single-cell imaging mass cytometry (IMC). Key findings were independently validated in an external single-cell RNA sequencing cohort. We identified 770 differentially methylated positions (P < 0.05, |logFC| <0.20) mapping to 386 genes that distinguish HPV-positive from HPV-negative tumors, with significant enrichment in immune-related pathways. Single-cell high-dimension IMC revealed distinct immune architectures between tumor types. In HPV-negative tumors, immune exclusion was primarily associated with fibroblast-dominated spatial organization that physically and functionally insulated tumor cells from immune surveillance. In contrast, T cells in HPV-positive tumors exhibited an intrinsic autocrine regulatory program characterized by robust type I and type II interferon signaling, consistent with enhanced tumor recognition and immune engagement. These findings demonstrate that HPV-associated DNA methylation reprogramming shapes the spatial and functional organization of the TME in HNC, promoting divergent mechanisms of immune regulation and tumor immune evasion.

title_zh: HPV驱动的DNA甲基化可塑性重塑头颈癌的免疫调节
source_body_en: Abstract The incidence of HPV-related HNC has exponentially increased over recent decades in head and neck cancer (HNC). Although HPV infection is known to reprogram the host epigenetic landscape, the cellular and functional consequences of HPV-mediated DNA methylation changes remain poorly defined. Here we demonstrated that HPV-driven epigenetic reprogramming reshapes immune regulation within the HNC tumor microenvironment (TME), generating distinct methylation landscapes associated with viral status. Genome-wide methylation analysis identified differentially methylated loci enriched in immune-related pathways, supporting a central role for epigenetic remodeling in shaping HPV-specific tumor–immune interactions. To link epigenetic differences to cellular organization and function within the TME, we characterized immune and stromal compartments, cell–cell interactions, and spatial architecture using high-dimensional single-cell imaging mass cytometry (IMC). Key findings were independently validated in an external single-cell RNA sequencing cohort. We identified 770 differentially methylated positions (P < 0.05, |logFC| <0.20) mapping to 386 genes that distinguish HPV-positive from HPV-negative tumors, with significant enrichment in immune-related pathways. Single-cell high-dimension IMC revealed distinct immune architectures between tumor types. In HPV-negative tumors, immune exclusion was primarily associated with fibroblast-dominated spatial organization that physically and functionally insulated tumor cells from immune surveillance. In contrast, T cells in HPV-positive tumors exhibited an intrinsic autocrine regulatory program characterized by robust type I and type II interferon signaling, consistent with enhanced tumor recognition and immune engagement. These findings demonstrate that HPV-associated DNA methylation reprogramming shapes the spatial and functional organization of the TME in HNC, promoting divergent mechanisms of immune regulation and tumor immune evasion.
abstract_zh: 摘要 近几十年来,头颈癌 (HNC) 中 HPV 相关 HNC 的 发病率 呈指数增长。尽管已知 HPV 感染会重新编程 宿主 表观遗传景观,但 HPV 介导的 DNA 甲基化变化的细胞和功能后果仍不清楚。在这里,我们证明了 HPV 驱动的表观遗传重编程重塑了 HNC 肿瘤微环境 (TME) 内的免疫调节,产生与病毒状态相关的独特甲基化景观。基因组 全甲基化分析鉴定出富含免疫相关途径的差异甲基化位点,支持表观遗传重塑在塑造 HPV 特异性肿瘤免疫相互作用中的核心作用。为了将表观遗传差异与 TME 内的细胞组织和功能联系起来,我们使用高维单细胞成像质谱流式仪 (IMC) 表征了免疫和基质区室、细胞间相互作用和空间结构。主要发现在外部单细胞 RNA 测序 队列研究 中得到独立验证。我们确定了 770 个差异甲基化位置(P < 0.05,|logFC| <0.20),映射到 386 个基因,区分 HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性肿瘤,并显着富集了免疫相关通路。单细胞高维 IMC 揭示了肿瘤类型之间不同的免疫结构。在 HPV 阴性肿瘤中,免疫排斥主要与成纤维细胞主导的空间组织相关,该空间组织在物理上和功能上将肿瘤细胞与免疫 监测 隔离。相比之下,HPV 阳性肿瘤中的 T 细胞表现出内在的自分泌调节程序,其特征是强大的 I 型和 II 型干扰素信号传导,与增强的肿瘤识别和免疫参与相一致。这些发现表明,HPV 相关的 DNA 甲基化重编程塑造了 HNC 中 TME 的空间和功能组织,促进免疫调节和肿瘤免疫逃避的不同机制。

title: HPV Prevalence, Subtype Distribution, and Vaccine-Associated Changes in Fuzhou Women Undergoing Health Examinations: An 11-Year Retrospective Study (2014–2025)
abstract: Abstract Background: To assess long-term trends in Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection rates, subtype distribution, and age-specific patterns before and after HPV vaccination in Fuzhou, China, to inform cervical cancer prevention. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 29,041 women (aged 16–79) who underwent HPV genotyping at Fuzhou University Affiliated Provincial Hospital from February 2014 to December 2025. Participants were grouped into pre-vaccination (2014–2017; n=18,542) and post-vaccination (2020–2025; n=10,499). Using fluorescent microsphere hybridization, 27 HPV subtypes (17 high-risk, 10 low-risk) were detected; overall positivity, high-/low-risk rates, and type-specific prevalence were compared. Age–infection probability was modeled using restricted cubic spline regression. Results: Overall HPV positivity was 15.77% (15.65% pre vs. 15.97% post; P=0.213). A persistent U-shaped age distribution was observed in both phases, peaking at ≤30 and ≥51 years (nadir 31-40). Post-vaccination, high-risk HPV decreased (14.49%→12.90%; RR=0.89; P<0.001), notably in the 31–40 group (RR=0.79); low-risk HPV increased (5.64% to 7.40%; RR=1.31; P<0.001), especially ≤30 years (RR=2.29). Bivalent-targeted types (HPV16/18) fell 48.0% and nine-valent-targeted types 13.4%, with greatest benefit at 31–40. Among young women, HPV16/18 declined while HPV6, HPV81, and HPV44 rose (HPV6 RR=4.24; HPV81 RR=3.17 in ≤30). Conclusions: HPV vaccination in Fuzhou reduced HPV16/18 prevalence, yet rising non-vaccine types (HPV6, HPV81) in young women suggest possible type replacement. Continued molecular surveillance, broader vaccines, and age-specific screening are warranted.

title_zh: 福州女性健康检查中HPV 患病率、亚型分布及疫苗相关变化:11年回顾性研究(2014-2025)
source_body_en: Abstract Background: To assess long-term trends in Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection rates, subtype distribution, and age-specific patterns before and after HPV vaccination in Fuzhou, China, to inform cervical cancer prevention. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed 29,041 women (aged 16–79) who underwent HPV genotyping at Fuzhou University Affiliated Provincial Hospital from February 2014 to December 2025. Participants were grouped into pre-vaccination (2014–2017; n=18,542) and post-vaccination (2020–2025; n=10,499). Using fluorescent microsphere hybridization, 27 HPV subtypes (17 high-risk, 10 low-risk) were detected; overall positivity, high-/low-risk rates, and type-specific prevalence were compared. Age–infection probability was modeled using restricted cubic spline regression. Results: Overall HPV positivity was 15.77% (15.65% pre vs. 15.97% post; P=0.213). A persistent U-shaped age distribution was observed in both phases, peaking at ≤30 and ≥51 years (nadir 31-40). Post-vaccination, high-risk HPV decreased (14.49%→12.90%; RR=0.89; P<0.001), notably in the 31–40 group (RR=0.79); low-risk HPV increased (5.64% to 7.40%; RR=1.31; P<0.001), especially ≤30 years (RR=2.29). Bivalent-targeted types (HPV16/18) fell 48.0% and nine-valent-targeted types 13.4%, with greatest benefit at 31–40. Among young women, HPV16/18 declined while HPV6, HPV81, and HPV44 rose (HPV6 RR=4.24; HPV81 RR=3.17 in ≤30). Conclusions: HPV vaccination in Fuzhou reduced HPV16/18 prevalence, yet rising non-vaccine types (HPV6, HPV81) in young women suggest possible type replacement. Continued molecular surveillance, broader vaccines, and age-specific screening are warranted.

title: MmuPV1 and HPV E6 Elevate Nuclear Accumulation of IKKɑ to Impair NF-κB Signaling to Promote Persistent Infection
abstract: Abstract The mouse papillomavirus (MmuPV1) E6 oncoprotein is essential for persistent infection and cancer development. Previous studies identified amino acid R130 of MmuPV1 E6 as critical for its interaction with the tumor suppressor MAML1. Mutation of this residue (R130A) disrupts MAML1 binding and prevents disease development in mice. In this study, we demonstrate that MmuPV1 E6 also disrupts NF-κB signaling through interactions with proteins in the IκB kinase (IKK) complex. Specifically, the MmuPV1 E6 R130A mutant is defective in binding IKK complex proteins and fails to impair NF-κB signaling in mouse keratinocytes, suggesting that these interactions are necessary for E6-mediated disruption of this pathway. Furthermore, MmuPV1 E6 expression is associated with increased nuclear localization of IKKɑ, whereas cells expressing the E6 R130A mutant exhibit no such increase. These findings suggest that E6-mediated nuclear localization of IKKɑ depends on its interaction with IKK complex proteins. Importantly, we demonstrate that the human papillomavirus HPV16 E6 oncoprotein similarly impairs NF-κB signaling and increases nuclear IKKɑ localization in human keratinocytes, suggesting a shared mechanism between mouse and human papillomaviruses. Additionally, analysis of previously published RNA sequencing data reveals that MmuPV1 E6 induces several transcriptional changes associated with increased nuclear IKKɑ. Together, these findings demonstrate that both MmuPV1 and HPV16 E6 disrupt NF-κB signaling in association with increased nuclear IKKɑ localization. This study provides the first evidence of an E6 oncoprotein interacting with and changing subcellular localization of IKKɑ to disrupt cellular homeostasis. Importance In this study, we demonstrate that the mouse papillomavirus (MmuPV1) E6 oncoprotein interacts with proteins of the inhibitor of κB kinase (IKK) complex to impair NF-κB signaling, a key cellular pathway involved in regulating processes such as the innate immune response. We find that the MmuPV1 E6 R130A mutant exhibits reduced binding to IKK complex proteins and a diminished ability to impair NF-κB signaling, highlighting the importance of these interactions. Notably, we demonstrate that HPV16 E6 similarly impairs NF-κB signaling in human keratinocytes, revealing a shared biological function between mouse and human papillomavirus E6 proteins. Furthermore, both MmuPV1 and HPV16 E6 promote increased nuclear localization of IKKɑ, which may contribute to disrupted NF-κB signaling. Analysis of previously published RNA sequencing data also reveals transcriptional changes associated with increased nuclear IKKɑ. Together, these findings identify a previously unrecognized interaction between E6 and IKKɑ that may contribute to disrupting cellular homeostasis.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the role of MmuPV1 E6 in disrupting NF-κB signaling, a key pathway in immune regulation, to understand its contribution to persistent infection and cancer development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved analysis of previously published RNA sequencing data and experiments with mouse and human keratinocytes expressing MmuPV1 E6 and its R130A mutant, focusing on the effects of these proteins on NF-κB signaling.
analysis.methods: The researchers analyzed previously published RNA sequencing data and conducted experiments to assess the interaction of MmuPV1 E6 with IKK complex proteins and its effect on nuclear localization of IKKɑ in keratinocytes.
analysis.main_results: MmuPV1 E6 expression was associated with increased nuclear localization of IKKɑ, while the R130A mutant failed to show this increase. Additionally, HPV16 E6 also promoted increased nuclear IKKɑ localization in human keratinocytes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that E6-mediated disruption of NF-κB signaling depends on its interaction with IKK complex proteins and that this mechanism may be conserved between mouse and human papillomaviruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the molecular mechanisms by which HPV E6 proteins disrupt immune pathways, which could inform future research on viral persistence and oncogenesis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on previously published RNA sequencing data and does not include direct experimental validation of the transcriptional changes, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how the E6 oncoprotein of mouse papillomavirus (MmuPV1) interacts with the IKK complex to impair NF-κB signaling, a critical pathway in immune regulation. The research demonstrates that MmuPV1 E6 promotes nuclear accumulation of IKKɑ, which is essential for its ability to disrupt cellular homeostasis and promote persistent infection. The study also reveals that the human papillomavirus HPV16 E6 oncoprotein exhibits a similar effect in human keratinocytes, suggesting a shared mechanism between mouse and human papillomaviruses. These findings highlight the importance of E6-IKK interactions in viral pathogenesis and provide a foundation for understanding how these interactions contribute to oncogenic processes. However, the reliance on existing RNA sequencing data limits the strength of the evidence to moderate, as direct experimental validation of the transcriptional changes was not performed.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查 MmuPV1 E6 在破坏 NF-κB 信号传导(免疫调节的关键途径)中的作用,以了解其对持续感染和癌症发展的贡献。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及对先前发表的 RNA 测序数据的分析以及对表达 MmuPV1 E6 及其 R130A 突变体的小鼠和人类角质形成细胞的实验,重点关注这些蛋白质对 NF-κB 信号传导的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究人员分析了之前发表的RNA测序数据,并进行了实验来评估MmuPV1 E6与IKK复合蛋白的相互作用及其对角质形成细胞中IKKɑ核定位的影响。
analysis_zh.main_results: MmuPV1 E6 表达与 IKKɑ 核定位增加相关,而 R130A 突变体未能显示出这种增加。此外,HPV16 E6 还促进人类角质形成细胞中 IKKɑ 核定位的增加。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,E6 介导的 NF-κB 信号传导破坏取决于其与 IKK 复合蛋白的相互作用,并且这种机制在小鼠和 人乳头瘤病毒 之间可能是保守的。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对 HPV E6 蛋白破坏免疫途径的分子机制的见解,这可以为未来关于病毒持久性和肿瘤发生的研究提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于之前发表的 RNA 测序数据,不包括转录变化的直接实验验证,将证据的强度限制为中等。

title: Understanding Cervical Screening Engagement Among Young South Asian Women: Perspectives of Women and Healthcare Professionals.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite increased uptake of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, cervical screening participation among younger South Asian women has declined, particularly in deprived areas in England. The reasons for this pattern remain poorly understood. This study explored barriers and facilitators to cervical screening among South Asian women aged 25-29 in a deprived locality. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with South Asian women aged 25-29 (n = 15) and healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery (n = 6) in Blackburn with Darwen. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Barriers to screening were multifactorial and included limited understanding of cervical screening and HPV, cultural norms surrounding modesty and sexuality, fear of community judgement and embarrassment, and structural challenges such as appointment access and competing responsibilities. Family networks acted as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals described adapting language to reduce fear, but highlighted service pressures related to staffing and funding, which constrained proactive engagement. Although most women reported receiving the HPV vaccination, understanding of HPV and the continued importance of cervical screening remained limited, highlighting opportunities to reinforce cervical screening education. CONCLUSION: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is shaped by intersecting cultural, emotional, and structural influences, which may be intensified in deprived settings. HPV vaccination should be accompanied by clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening, particularly where knowledge and awareness remain low. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision and community partnership approaches are needed to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was informed by prior community engagement and public involvement work with underserved populations. Interview guides were developed in collaboration with a public advisor from the South Asian community to ensure they were relevant, inclusive, and reflective of community priorities.

title_zh: 了解南亚年轻女性的宫颈筛查参与度:女性和医疗保健专业人员的观点。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Despite increased uptake of the human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine, cervical screening participation among younger South Asian women has declined, particularly in deprived areas in England. The reasons for this pattern remain poorly understood. This study explored barriers and facilitators to cervical screening among South Asian women aged 25-29 in a deprived locality. METHODS: Semi-structured interviews were conducted with South Asian women aged 25-29 (n = 15) and healthcare professionals involved in cervical screening delivery (n = 6) in Blackburn with Darwen. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS: Barriers to screening were multifactorial and included limited understanding of cervical screening and HPV, cultural norms surrounding modesty and sexuality, fear of community judgement and embarrassment, and structural challenges such as appointment access and competing responsibilities. Family networks acted as both barriers and facilitators. Healthcare professionals described adapting language to reduce fear, but highlighted service pressures related to staffing and funding, which constrained proactive engagement. Although most women reported receiving the HPV vaccination, understanding of HPV and the continued importance of cervical screening remained limited, highlighting opportunities to reinforce cervical screening education. CONCLUSION: Cervical screening engagement among young South Asian women is shaped by intersecting cultural, emotional, and structural influences, which may be intensified in deprived settings. HPV vaccination should be accompanied by clear communication about the continued importance of cervical screening, particularly where knowledge and awareness remain low. Culturally responsive communication, flexible service provision and community partnership approaches are needed to address persistent inequalities in screening uptake. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The study was informed by prior community engagement and public involvement work with underserved populations. Interview guides were developed in collaboration with a public advisor from the South Asian community to ensure they were relevant, inclusive, and reflective of community priorities.
abstract_zh: 背景:尽管 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 疫苗 的使用率有所增加,但南亚年轻女性的宫颈筛查参与率有所下降,特别是在英格兰的贫困地区。造成这种模式的原因仍然知之甚少。本研究探讨了贫困地区 25-29 岁南亚女性宫颈筛查的障碍和促进因素。方法:与 Darwen 一起对布莱克本 25-29 岁的南亚女性 (n = 15) 和参与宫颈筛查的医疗保健专业人员 (n = 6) 进行半结构化访谈。使用反思性主题分析对数据进行分析。结果:筛查的障碍是多因素的,包括对宫颈筛查和 HPV 的了解有限、关于谦虚和性的文化规范、对社区判断和尴尬的恐惧,以及预约机会和竞争责任等结构性挑战。家庭网络既是障碍又是促进者。医疗保健专业人员描述了调整语言以减少恐惧,但强调了与人员配置和资金相关的服务压力,这限制了积极参与。尽管大多数女性报告接受了 HPV 疫苗接种,但对 HPV 和宫颈筛查的持续重要性的了解仍然有限,这凸显了加强宫颈筛查教育的机会。结论:南亚年轻女性的宫颈筛查参与度受到文化、情感和结构等交叉影响的影响,这种影响在贫困环境中可能会加剧。HPV 疫苗接种 应伴随着关于宫颈筛查的持续重要性的明确沟通,特别是在知识和意识仍然较低的情况下。需要采取文化敏感的沟通、灵活的服务提供和社区伙伴关系方法来解决筛查方面持续存在的不平等问题。患者或公众贡献:该研究是根据先前的社区参与和针对服务不足人群的公众参与工作而进行的。访谈指南是与南亚社区的公共顾问合作制定的,以确保它们具有相关性、包容性并反映社区的优先事项。

title: Preimplementation Factors for a Mobile Decision Support Tool for Cervical Cancer Screening Among Dominican Women Living With HIV: Qualitative Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT: Women living with HIV (WLH) have a sixfold greater risk of cervical cancer. In the Dominican Republic, cervical cancer and HIV remain prevalent, yet screening rates are low. The World Health Organization recommends a same-day screening, triage, and treatment protocol for WLH, but implementation faces persistent barriers. This study examined barriers and facilitators to implementing iSTAR, a mobile clinical decision support tool designed to guide providers through the screening, triage, and treatment protocol through rapid human papillomavirus DNA testing and results interpretation. We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis guided by the Health Equity Implementation Framework of transcripts from 16 providers and 25 WLH across formative interviews and usability testing. Societal, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors intersected during clinical encounters to shape implementation, indicating that neither protocol adoption nor technology alone will sustain implementation. Findings support multilevel strategies for successful initial and sustained implementation.
journal: The Journal of the Association of Nurses in AIDS Care : JANAC

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand barriers and facilitators to implementing a mobile decision support tool for cervical cancer screening among Dominican women living with HIV, given the high risk of cervical cancer in this population.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved a secondary qualitative analysis of transcripts from 16 providers and 25 women living with HIV across formative interviews and usability testing in the Dominican Republic.
analysis_en.methods: The analysis was guided by the Health Equity Implementation Framework and focused on sociocultural, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors that intersected during clinical encounters.
analysis_en.main_results: Findings indicated that multilevel strategies are necessary for successful initial and sustained implementation of the screening, triage, and treatment protocol.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlighted the importance of addressing societal, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors to ensure the successful implementation of the mobile decision support tool.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that a comprehensive approach is needed to improve cervical cancer screening rates among women living with HIV, emphasizing the need for multilevel strategies.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the secondary nature of the analysis and the potential for bias in the qualitative data, but the evidence suggests a high level of confidence in the findings.

title_zh: 用于在多米尼加艾滋病毒感染者中进行 宫颈癌 筛查的移动决策支持工具的预实施因素:定性研究。
source_body_en: ABSTRACT: Women living with HIV (WLH) have a sixfold greater risk of cervical cancer. In the Dominican Republic, cervical cancer and HIV remain prevalent, yet screening rates are low. The World Health Organization recommends a same-day screening, triage, and treatment protocol for WLH, but implementation faces persistent barriers. This study examined barriers and facilitators to implementing iSTAR, a mobile clinical decision support tool designed to guide providers through the screening, triage, and treatment protocol through rapid human papillomavirus DNA testing and results interpretation. We conducted a secondary qualitative analysis guided by the Health Equity Implementation Framework of transcripts from 16 providers and 25 WLH across formative interviews and usability testing. Societal, clinic-level, patient, and provider factors intersected during clinical encounters to shape implementation, indicating that neither protocol adoption nor technology alone will sustain implementation. Findings support multilevel strategies for successful initial and sustained implementation.
abstract_zh: 摘要:感染艾滋病毒 (WLH) 的女性患 宫颈癌 的风险增加六倍。在多米尼加共和国,宫颈癌 和艾滋病毒仍然流行,但筛查率较低。世界卫生组织建议对 WLH 采取当日筛查、分诊和 治疗 方案,但实施面临持续的障碍。这项研究探讨了实施 iSTAR 的障碍和促进因素,iSTAR 是一种移动临床决策支持工具,旨在通过快速 人乳头瘤病毒 DNA 测试和结果解释来指导提供者完成筛查、分类和 治疗 协议。我们在健康公平实施框架的指导下,对 16 家提供者和 25 家 WLH 的形成性访谈和可用性测试的成绩单进行了二次定性分析。在临床实践中,社会、诊所层面、患者和提供者因素相互交叉影响实施,这表明无论是协议的采用还是技术本身都无法维持实施。研究结果支持成功的初步和持续实施的多层次战略。

title: Intratumoral CD8+ T-cell differentiation is linked to durable HPV-specific immunity after neoadjuvant HPV vaccination with long-acting IL-7 and PD-1 blockade
abstract: Abstract Durable antigen-specific immunity is a goal of therapeutic vaccination, but its relationship to intratumoral CD8+ T-cell differentiation remains poorly defined. To address this question, we compared anti–PD-1, tirvalimogene teraplasmid (GX-188E), and long-acting IL-7 (GX-I7/NT-I7), alone and in combination, in HPV-positive tumor-bearing mice. Among tested regimens, triple immunotherapy produced the greatest tumor control and a pooled tumor profile enriched for stemness-associated intratumoral CD8+ states. We then evaluated the same components in a four-cohort phase 2 neoadjuvant study of 56 patients with resectable HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. In the 11-patient cohort receiving pembrolizumab, GX-188E, and NT-I7, 7 patients had a major pathologic response, including 4 with a pathologic complete response. To define the intratumoral immune program accompanying this activity, paired tumor profiling identified a GZMK+ effector-memory CD8+ state with cytotoxicity- and memory-associated features. GZMK+ effector-memory cells were prominent among T cells bearing clonotypes shared between post-treatment tumors and tumor-draining lymph nodes, consistent with intercompartmental recirculation. Higher tdLN Myc expression in both NT-I7-containing mouse profiles prompted regulatory analysis of the human GZMK+ state, revealing treatment-associated higher MYC and lower BATF regulon specificity; in silico IL7R perturbation was consistent with an IL-7-associated reprogramming model. Post-treatment intratumoral MYC-associated and relative MYC/BATF regulon measures were related to HPV16 E6/E7-reactive activation-induced marker responses at 2 years; in eight patients with paired tumors, treatment-associated relative MYC/BATF changes were separately related to a 2-year peptide-responsive CD8+ stem cell–like memory phenotype. Together, these findings associate intratumoral GZMK+ effector-memory remodeling with HPV-reactive activation and memory phenotypes 2 years later.

We then evaluated the same components in a four-cohort phase 2 neoadjuvant study of 56 patients with resectable HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. In the 11-patient cohort receiving pembrolizumab, GX-188E, and NT-I7, 7 patients had a major pathologic response, including 4 with a pathologic complete response. To define the intratumoral immune program accompanying this activity, paired tumor profiling identified a GZMK+ effector-memory CD8+ state with cytotoxicity- and memory-associated features. Higher tdLN Myc expression in both NT-I7-containing mouse profiles prompted regulatory analysis of the human GZMK+ state, revealing treatment-associated higher MYC and lower BATF regulon specificity; in silico IL7R perturbation was consistent with an IL-7-associated reprogramming model. Together, these findings associate intratumoral GZMK+ effector-memory remodeling with HPV-reactive activation and memory phenotypes 2 years later.

abstract_zh: 摘要 持久的抗原特异性免疫是 疫苗接种 治疗的目标,但其与瘤内 CD8+ T 细胞分化的关系仍不清楚。为了解决这个问题,我们在 HPV 阳性荷瘤小鼠中比较了单独和联合使用的抗 PD-1、tirvalimogene teraplasmid (GX-188E) 和长效 IL-7 (GX-I7/NT-I7)。在测试的方案中,三重免疫疗法产生了最大的肿瘤控制和丰富的干性相关瘤内 CD8+ 状态的汇总肿瘤谱。然后,我们在一项 4-队列研究 2 期新辅助研究中评估了相同的成分,该研究纳入了 56 名可切除 HPV 阳性头颈鳞状细胞癌患者。在接受派姆单抗、GX-188E 和 NT-I7 治疗的 11 名患者 队列研究 中,7 名患者出现主要病理缓解,其中 4 名患者出现病理完全缓解。为了定义伴随该活动的肿瘤内免疫程序,配对肿瘤分析鉴定了具有细胞毒性和记忆相关特征的 GZMK+ 效应记忆 CD8+ 状态。GZMK+效应记忆细胞在治疗后肿瘤和肿瘤引流淋巴结之间共享克隆型的T细胞中最为突出,这与间室再循环一致。在两种含有 NT-I7 的小鼠中,较高的 tdLN Myc 表达促进了对人类 GZMK+ 状态的调节分析,揭示了 治疗 相关的较高 MYC 和较低 BATF 调节子特异性;计算机模拟 IL7R 扰动与 IL-7 相关重编程模型一致。治疗 后肿瘤内 MYC 相关和相对 MYC/BATF 调节子测量与 2 年时 HPV16 E6/E7 反应性激活诱导的标志物反应相关;在 8 名患有配对肿瘤的患者中,治疗 相关的相对 MYC/BATF 变化分别与 2 年肽反应性 CD8+ 干细胞样记忆表型相关。总之,这些发现将瘤内 GZMK+ 效应记忆重塑与 2 年后的 HPV 反应性激活和记忆表型联系起来。

title: Same margin, different lesion: margin subtype, glandular involvement, and endocervical curettage status as predictors of residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure: An 11-year retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess how initial loop electrosurgical excision procedure margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and specimen size relate to re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology and receipt of further surgery. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 287 patients undergoing re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure at a tertiary center (2015-2025) were reviewed. Initial margin status was classified as margin continuity, margin adjacency, or non-evaluable margin. Associations with re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology, residual CIN2+ disease, and receipt of a third surgical intervention were assessed using chi-square/Fisher-Freeman-Halton tests, Cohen's kappa, and multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: Initial and re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology showed a significant group-level association (p=0.039) but no case-by-case agreement beyond chance (kappa=-0.009, p=0.754); most patients with initial CIN2/3 had CIN1 at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure. Margin adjacency independently predicted residual CIN2+ disease at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure (OR 11.045, p=0.049), as did glandular involvement (OR 1.938, p=0.035). Among patients with negative re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure margins, residual CIN2+ disease was identified within the specimen in 27.1%, and human papillomavirus test negativity at the first follow-up visit was 88.2%, varying by genotype. Positive margin (OR 333.33, p<0.001) and positive endocervical curettage (OR 41.67, p<0.001) at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure were the strongest predictors of receiving a third surgical intervention. CONCLUSION: Margin adjacency and glandular involvement independently predicted residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure, whereas positive margins and positive endocervical curettage at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure were strongly associated with receipt of a third surgical intervention. Post-loop electrosurgical excision procedure follow-up should integrate margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and human papillomavirus surveillance rather than rely on margin status alone; genotype-specific differences in human papillomavirus test negativity require confirmation in larger cohorts.

title: HPV Oncogenes rewire DNA crosslink repair to create a PRIMPOL-dependent therapeutic vulnerability
abstract: Cisplatin-based chemoradiation is the standard of care for both HPV-negative (HPV−) and HPV-positive (HPV+) head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC), even though patients with HPV+ tumors have better treatment responses and a better prognosis. Understanding how HPV status shapes this response could guide alternative strategies that lower long-term toxicity. Using genome-wide CRISPR screens, we show that the genetic requirements for surviving chemoradiation diverge between HPV− and HPV+ HNSCC cells. HPV+ cells tolerate cisplatin-induced interstrand crosslinks independently of the Fanconi anemia pathway, a phenotype recapitulated by expressing HPV16 E6 and E7 in an HPV-negative background. In these cells, DNA damage tolerance depends instead on PRIMPOL-mediated repriming and post-replicative gap filling by translesion synthesis polymerases. Although they recruit BRCA1 normally to double-strand breaks, BRCA1 accumulation at cisplatin-stalled forks is markedly reduced, indicating that BRCA1 function is uncoupled between these two substrates. This tolerance pathway leaves cells dependent on dynamic RAD51 turnover at single-stranded DNA gaps. Depletion of the RAD51 unloading factor FIRRM, or chemical stabilization of RAD51 filaments, selectively kills HPV+ and HPV oncogene-expressing cells treated with cisplatin, and PRIMPOL depletion rescues this lethality. Our findings show that HPV oncogenes rewire the response to crosslink-induced replication stress and identify RAD51 filament dynamics as a therapeutic vulnerability in HPV+ HNSCC.

title: Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification-Assisted Rapid, Accurate, and Sensitive Photoelectrochemical Biosensing With CdIn 2 S 4 /SnS Heterojunction Quenched by Methylene Blue.
abstract: ABSTRACT Rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV‐16) is highly significant for early cervical cancer intervention. Herein, a novel loop‐mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP)‐assisted photoelectrochemical (PEC) biosensor is rationally constructed with type II heterojunction CdIn 2 S 4 /SnS (CIS/SS) quenched by methylene blue (MB). With the superior charge separation of CIS/SS, an intense initial photocurrent is obtained. After intercalating into double‐stranded DNA products of efficient LAMP, residual free MB is rapidly and directly immobilized on CIS/SS via electrostatic and chemical adsorption (15 min), causing remarkable photocurrent quenching. This finding not only circumvents tedious and time‐consuming quenching probe modification, but also shortens the mutual distance with significantly improved quenching efficiency over traditional ones. More importantly, mechanistic investigations innovatively reveal that photogenerated electrons preferentially transfer from CIS to MB over SS, triggering MB reduction. Meanwhile, adsorbed MB exerts a light‐shielding effect to reduce incident light reaching CIS/SS, collectively causing remarkable photocurrent quenching for enhanced sensitivity with a wide linear range from 1 fM to 1 nM and a detection limit of 0.70 fM. Besides constructing a reliable PEC sensing platform for rapid HPV‐16 detection, this work profoundly clarifies the synergistic quenching mechanism of MB, offering theoretical support for various high‐performance PEC quenching biosensors.

title: Editorial: Impact of gut probiotic metabolites on human metabolic diseases
abstract: irritable bowel syndrome, a multifactorial disorder with abdominal pain, altered bowel habits and multifaceted interactions among the gut microbiome. The importance of evaluating probiotic efficiency at the strain level rather than at the species level, with particular emphasis on their metabolites, notably short-chain fatty acids, is highlighted. Inadequate dietary control and incomplete strain, dose, and biomarker assessments limit the application of probiotics for IBD (Mora Guzmán et al., 2026) .The effects of probiotics, Lactobacillus plantarum strain LP-115 and Bifidobacterium bifidum strain BB-06, on gut microbiota functions were investigated among liver failure cases. Rats supplemented with probiotics showed increased levels of SCFAs and decreased levels of toxic metabolites, such as ammonia. Shotgun metagenomic reconstruction of faecal DNA provided comprehensive insights into the metabolic potential of the microbiome (Luo et al., 2026).The effect of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG, Lactobacillus plantarum, and Bifidobacterium longum on intestinal barrier function and hepatic injury in an animal model of fulminant liver failure (FLF) has been reported in this study. Probiotic treatment reduced intestinal hyperpermeability and restored tight junction integrity. In addition, probiotics reduced serum levels of alanine aminotransferase, aspartate aminotransferase, bilirubin, ammonia, oxidative stress markers and pro-inflammatory cytokines.Histopathological examination of liver tissue showed reduced hepatocellular injury and apoptosis.Probiotics may represent an effective therapeutic approach for protecting against FLF (C. Wu et al., 2026).Random forest models classified disease stages with 89.3% accuracy and identified key microbial markers, providing microbiome signatures as potential diagnostic, severity, and personalized therapeutic tools for H. pylori-related diseases. pylori eradication therapy along with probiotics might enhance eradication rates, reduce the side effects associated with antibiotics, help to preserve gut and oral microbiota and support their use as adjunctive therapy (X. Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 reduces IL-6 and TNF-α levels, increases intestinal occludin expression, and improves gut microbial composition and diversity in a rat model of sepsis. It stimulated the growth of beneficial bacteria and inhibited the growth of harmful bacteria, suggesting a potential to block disruption of the intestinal barrier and inflammation (Liu et al., 2025).In a double-blind randomized controlled trial, probiotics improved irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) symptoms by modulating increased fecal acetate, propionate, and butyrate levels; enhancing intestinal barrier integrity and tight-junction protein expression; and decreasing inflammation. Higher SCFA levels were associated with symptom improvement, highlighting the possible role of SCFAs in probiotic benefits. Overall, probiotics seem safe and effective for treating IBS through SCFA production, barrier strengthening, and anti-inflammatory effects (E. A network metaanalysis of 29 randomized controlled trials with 4,389 patients showed that fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) had the best improvement in bowel movements and stool consistency and acupuncture had a good clinical response. Probiotics had the lowest risk of adverse events. This study supports FMT, with or without acupuncture, as a promising treatment for functional constipation, but further high-quality studies are needed (Tan et al., 2025).The gut microbiome is a key factor influencing host energy metabolism. The review highlights the role of probiotic-fermented herbal residues in managing obesity by revealing the biological processes that improve bioactive compounds and their bioavailability by modulating the gut-liver axis. The combined herbal medicine and modern biotechnology will be a promising approach for managing metabolic disorders (Tian et al., 2026). The multi-omics approach assessed the impact of probiotic supplementation on gut microbiota composition and metabolomic profiles in women with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).Administration of Lactobacillus and Bifidobacterium significantly changed the gut microbiota and increased the levels of SCFAs, particularly butyrate and acetate. Gene expression analysis using RT-PCR showed a 2.5-to 1.9-fold increase in insulin receptor and AKT expression, suggesting greater insulin sensitivity; however, gut barrier genes (ZO-1 and CLDN1) also increased. Probiotic supplementation may be a non-invasive, safer therapeutic approach for GDM by improving insulin sensitivity and gut health (Su et al., 2026).The meta-analysis covers 46 randomized controlled trials with 3,580 participants with either type 1 or type 2 diabetes. Probiotic/synbiotic administration significantly decreased CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α, along with increased IL-10 and SCFA levels. Probiotic/synbiotic and SCFA supplementation may be a better diabetes care strategy (Xie et al., 2025).Another meta-analysis showed that microbial metabolites from probiotics interact with host proteins and tissue-specific pathways affecting gastrointestinal and metabolic health. Network and transcriptomic analyzes revealed important metabolite-gene relationships involving 10-hydroxy-cis-12-octadecenoic acid, glycodeoxycholic acid and N-(1-carbamoyl-2-phenyl-ethyl) butyramide. These findings identify molecular connections between microbial metabolites and host function that can inform microbiome-directed therapies and precision nutrition approaches to improve metabolic health (Yao et al., 2025).Potential host targets and biological functions of probiotic-based metabolites were identified using an integrative network-based approach based on metabolite-protein interactions and tissue-specific transcriptomics. High-degree genes including SLC27A4, LCN12 and APOD were highly expressed in gastrointestinal tract tissues, suggesting their involvement in host-microbe interactions. Metabolitespecific analysis showed different expression patterns. 10-hydroxy-cis-12-octadecenoic acid demonstrated a relationship to sialyltransferases and neuraminidase, glycodeoxycholic acid was related to bile acid metabolism and lipid transport and N-(1-carbamoyl-2-phenyl-ethyl) butyramide was related to detoxification pathways (Ma & Zhang, 2025).The systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the effectiveness of probiotic-derived metabolitetargeted interventions on hormonal and metabolic outcomes in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). Experimental treatments included synbiotics, probiotics, sodium butyrate, Akkermansia muciniphila, and short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) compositions, and all interventions lasted at least 8 weeks. Pooled data analysis showed a significant decrease in total testosterone, LH/FSH, fasting insulin, and HOMA-IR, with a slight increase in HDL cholesterol (Maddirevula et al., 2025).A total of 46 randomized controlled trials involving more than 12,500 pregnant women suggest that probiotic supplementation may reduce gestational weight gain and postpartum weight retention and improve fasting glucose, HOMA-IR, total cholesterol, and LDL. This study reveals that probiotics are a promising non-pharmacological strategy for improving maternal metabolic health and reducing adverse pregnancy outcomes in obese women through multiple pathways (Jia et al., 2025).A randomized double-blind and placebo-controlled trial assessed multistrain probiotics (Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and Bifidobacterium longum) administered to 84 subjects who had closed tibial shaft fractures, through 3-dimensional microcomputed tomography (CT) measurements of BV/TV. Exploratory analyses showed that probiotics were associated with earlier weight-bearing, reduced pain at week 2, and higher RUST scores at 12 weeks. These results suggest that perioperative probiotic administration could not only promote fracture healing but also accelerate functional recovery, likely mediated by gut-bone axis-based immunomodulatory effects. Thus, probiotics can positively impact fracture care as an adjunct to standard treatment (Huang et al., 2026).Another study explored the role of probiotics in sarcopenia using data from NHANES and the UK Biobank, integrated with in vitro C2C12 myotube experiments, molecular docking, and machinelearning models. Individuals who regularly consume probiotics have higher handgrip strength and fatfree mass, and lower signs of inflammation, than those who do not. Probiotic-conditioned media greatly promoted muscle cell fusion, increased cell diameter, and increased expression of the muscle regulatory genes MyoD, Myogenin, and MyHC; it also reduced NF-κB and TNF-α while boosting PGC-1 levels. Butyrate showed strong interactions with AMPK, mTOR and NF-B. Thus, probiotics could help preserve muscle via immune responses and microbiota-controlled metabolic and muscleanabolism pathways (Wang et al., 2026).The study evaluated the impact of gut microbiome changes on postoperative recovery in postmenopausal women by examining stool samples using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and QIIME2.Analysis of alpha and beta diversity exhibited major changes in microbial composition, with a predominance of Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, associated with improved functional outcomes and faster recovery. Conversely, Proteobacteria and Escherichia were linked to delayed healing and worse clinical outcomes. Based on microbial abundance, a random forest machine learning model achieved 85% accuracy in predicting clinical recovery, suggesting that gut microbiome signatures may serve as key biomarkers and provide a basis for microbiome-based personalized strategies to accelerate postoperative recovery and enhance long-term musculoskeletal health. Furthermore, microbiome composition correlates with various important surgical parameters such as bone healing and infection rate (Pan et al., 2026).A meta-analysis evaluated the effects of different doses and intervention durations of different probiotic strains on bone metabolism. The review states that probiotic supplementation boosts bone formation and decreases bone resorption in patients with osteoporosis. Formulations with probiotic consortia and higher doses showed significant improvements, especially in postmenopausal women, suggesting that probiotics may be a promising adjunctive approach to improve bone health. The changes observed in bone resorption markers indicate the beneficial effects of probiotics on bone health. Probiotics are not considered a primary treatment for osteoporosis, but could support maintaining bone health (Yuan et al., 2026).The human gastrointestinal tract (GIT) is colonized by a complex microbial community which plays major roles in host physiology, metabolism, immunity and neurobehavioral functions. This study highlights the bidirectional gut-brain axis, in which the gut microbiota influences neural signalling, stress responses, and emotional regulation. Dysbiosis of this gut microbiota has been linked with psychiatric, neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders such as anxiety, autism spectrum disorder, major depressive disorder, and schizophrenia. Psychobiotics are promising microbiomebased interventions for supporting mental health. These benefits may arise from modulation of neurotransmitter production, SCFA signaling, immune responses, and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity. FMT restores the natural gut microbiota and relieves the symptoms of mental illness via modulating inflammatory pathways. These emerging therapies, psychobiotics and FMT, may be promising strategies for managing mental health disorders (Selta et al., 2026).The study assessed the effect of washed microbiota transplantation (WMT) and investigated the changes in gut microbiota in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Thirty-eight ASD children who underwent a full course of WMT from a single donor were evaluated before and 4 weeks after treatment by clinical rating scales and 16S rRNA gene sequencing. WMT significantly improved core ASD symptoms, sleep, and GI symptoms. In addition, the therapeutic effect was related to the gut microbiota of both the donor and recipient before therapy, suggesting that donor-recipient microbiota compatibility may influence the effect of WMT in ASD (Quan et al., 2026).The multi-omics study provides mechanistic evidence supporting the neuromodulatory effect of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG and Bifidobacterium longum 1714. rhamnosus GG mainly boosts GABAergic and SCFA-based synaptic pathways, whereas B. longum 1714 influences the tryptophanserotonin-immune axis. Additionally, in vitro validation demonstrated increased GABA and serotonin release, reduced ROS levels, and enrichment of anti-inflammatory transcripts in EVs. These findings reveal the therapeutic potential of L. longum 1714 for neurological health (Jin et al., 2026).The effect of Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG was evaluated in sepsis-induced lung injury by assessing the gut-lung axis. Probiotic supplementation in Wistar rats endangered by caecal ligation and puncture improved pulmonary function, lung histology, and respiratory parameters. Probiotic culture also restored the gut microbiota and reduced hypoxemia and inflammation. Thus, efficient therapeutic probiotics will greatly increase the success of treatment and improve the patient's quality of life and survival (Wang et al., 2026).A single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated the effects of probiotic lozenges in children with adenoid hypertrophy and otitis media with effusion receiving standard nonsurgical management. Probiotic treatment significantly improved tympanogram classification compared with placebo, with favorable changes in tympanometric and audiological parameters, including DPOAE conversion. Probiotic treatment may improve auditory function by promoting probiotic colonization and inhibiting pathogens, supporting the potential of probiotic bacteria as a safe adjunct for conservative management of pediatric otitis media with effusion (Shi et al., 2026).Network pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis identified 110 gut microbiota-derived metabolites with 6,860 potential human target genes and 268 overlapping otitis media associated genes. Enrichment analyzes of these targets to inflammatory and immune pathways provided molecular evidence for microbial metabolites as candidate therapeutics (Zheng & Jin, 2025). Reanalysis of the public dataset GSE43764 identified the effect of oral Lactobacillus pentosus B240 on innate immunity against H1N1 influenza via modulation of the glutathione-ROS pathway and the macrophage type I IFN axis. Probiotic supplementation was associated with improved baseline antioxidant and oxidative stress regulatory pathways, associated with coordinated activation of GSH-ROS, Nrf2, macrophage activation and type I IFN responses. Differential and co-expression analyzes showed regulated expression of genes involved in glutathione metabolism, oxidative stress, macrophage activity, interferon signaling, and antiviral defense. Mixed probiotics significantly reduced lung damage and pathological inflammation and enhanced immune cell function and systemic immune response (Ye & Zhang, 2025).The therapeutic potential of probiotics, Lactobacillus rhamnosus, L. plantarum, and Bifidobacterium longum, along with their heat-killed preparations, extracellular vesicles, and metabolite extracts, to control HPV-associated head and neck cancer is demonstrated using microbiome, immunological, and computational approaches. Probiotic treatment improved immune regulation and epithelial barrier function and decreased cancer cell viability by inducing apoptosis. Their therapeutic potential was also supported by increased caspase activity and immunoregulatory cytokines. These results suggest that live probiotic cultures and their various forms and metabolites could be promising adjunctive therapies for HPV-associated head and neck cancer (Jiang et al., 2026).A randomized controlled trial (RCT) investigated the effects of comprehensive nursing care combined with probiotic intervention on improving gut health in patients with malignancies. After 8 weeks of intervention, the observation group had better gastrointestinal function and nutritional status, reduced non-infectious complications and improved quality of life among patients undergoing chemotherapy.This study found therapeutic value in probiotics combined with comprehensive nursing care for patients with gastrointestinal malignancies (Huang et al., 2026).The retrospective study investigated how a probiotic-rich diet combined with an enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) nursing pathway, affects postoperative recovery in patients with laryngeal cancer.The treatment with probiotic formulation containing Lactobacillus acidophilus LA-5, Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. Lactis BB12 led to higher recovery rates in energy and protein intake in the early postoperative phase through the gastrointestinal tract. Inflammatory markers CRP, IL-6, and leukocyte count had increased, and albumin and prealbumin levels had declined. The probability of complications, including pneumonia, wound infection and pharyngocutaneous fistula, was much reduced. Hospital stay and antibiotic use were reduced (Wei et al., 2025).In this meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials with 1,246 women with endometrial cancer (EC), probiotics increased gut microbiota diversity, increased beneficial bacteria, and reduced gastrointestinal complications. Probiotics also improved well-being and reduced IL-6 and TNF-α levels. Multi-strain formulations, higher doses (≥1010 CFU/day) and longer interventions had greater benefits, supporting probiotics as a potential adjunctive therapy (Chen et al., 2025).This review explores the significant role of Akkermansia muciniphila, an important gut commensal, in maintaining gut immune homeostasis and metabolic balance. The molecular mechanisms underlying the anti-inflammatory effects of A. muciniphila involve intestinal barrier enhancement, immune modulation, metabolite-mediated signaling and reshaping the gut microbiota. This review also notes that pasteurized preparations and bioactive metabolites can have therapeutic effects alongside live bacterial cultures (Xie et al., 2026). This review highlights the phenylketonuria pathophysiology, gut probiotics, phenylalanine amino acid metabolism, and the therapeutic potential of probiotics. Pre-and probiotic-based approaches could benefit phenylketonuria treatment by increasing microbial diversity and making the microbiome more resilient, enabling the intestine to resist disturbances and prevent losses in functional diversity (Kalla Veedu et al., 2025).Though gut microbiome and their metabolites ae gaining more attention and popularity, the interpretation and therapeutic strategy of the available data are limited due to less availability of clinical translations. Molecular docking, computational projections, and in vitro investigations provide mechanistic insights, but they do not adequately replicate physiological circumstances or prove clinical relevance. Such in silico studies require experimental validation for identified biomarkers and predicted metabolite-protein interactions. Clinical consequences are not always causally linked to changes in microbial abundance or metabolite concentrations. It is yet unclear how microbial metabolites, live probiotics, microbial consortia, and host responses relate to one another. Furthermore, conclusions drawn from certain strains, formulations and disease models cannot be applied to all probiotic treatments. In this research topic, the published in vitro and in silico studies indicate potential probiotic activities, metabolites, host targets and biological pathways but cannot be used to establish a therapeutic efficacy per se. Reported animal studies suggest potential physiologic effects of B. fragilis, such as modulation of inflammation, injury to organs, intestinal barrier integrity and microbial metabolism, but these findings need to be validated in human volunteers. Human studies and clinical trials provide more direct evidence of clinical relevance, but limitations related to sample size, duration of the study, differences in populations, and outcome measures must be considered. Together, these complementary categories of evidence underscore the importance of mechanistic validation, reproducible preclinical findings, and sufficiently driven clinical trials for demonstrating efficacy and safety of probiotic mediations.The 32 articles published in this research topic collectively provide understanding of the potential roles of the gut microbiome, probiotics and their metabolites in human health. The findings reports recurring themes, including host metabolism, inflammatory signalling, intestinal barrier function, microbial community structure, and gut-organ communication. Conversely, the evidence provided differs between studies, disease perspectives, and outcomes, and study benefits are not equivalent to proven clinical efficiency. Moreover, research underscore and standard preclinical and clinical trial and in safety microbiome based approaches require reproducible functional and benefits for that they do not have of on this that they were an of research topic of Probiotic on Human of in and This had impact on review and the

title: Single-Particle ICP-MS Enabled Multiplex Digital Detection of Nucleic Acids via Feedback Recombinase Polymerase Amplification.
abstract: Digital droplet assays, with their single-molecule sensitivity, hold great promise for early disease diagnosis by enabling precise biomarker quantification and the generation of patient-specific molecular profiles. Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) has shown its great potential in the quantification of biomolecules with elemental labeling strategies. However, the development of ICP-MS-based digital assays has been limited, primarily due to the challenge of efficiently anchoring elemental labels within droplets. To address this, we developed a feedback recombinase polymerase amplification (F-RPA)-based digital analyzer via a facile droplet generator and combined it with single particle (sp)-ICP-MS for the quantitative analysis of human papillomavirus (HPV) genetic markers. In this system, HPV DNA molecules are randomly partitioned across tens of thousands of agarose droplets, following a Poisson distribution. Individual encapsulated target DNA molecules initiate on-demand F-RPA amplification and anchoring of elemental tags for subsequent signal transduction. Leveraging the discrete event counting characteristics and multi-element analytical capabilities of sp-ICP-MS, the digital F-RPA assay achieved highly sensitive and multiplexed analysis, with detection limits as low as 20 copies/μL for HPV16 and 9 copies/μL for HPV18 DNA. The method was validated by quantifying the HPV DNA load in cervical cancer cell lines and further applied to clinical cervical swab samples, where it identified 26 HPV16-positive and 20 HPV18-positive cases with 100% precision. This digital F-RPA sp-ICP-MS system emerges as a robust diagnostic platform for trace biomarker analysis, significantly advancing the role of sp-ICP-MS in digital droplet detection and clinical diagnosis.

title: A Multidimensional Framework to Combat HPV Vaccine Misinformation in the Digital Age: Implications for Cervical Cancer Prevention
abstract: Abstract Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a cornerstone of cervical cancer prevention, yet its uptake remains constrained by misinformation and myths amplified through social media worldwide. Combating this digital infodemic requires an integrated public health response that unites behavioral science, artificial intelligence (AI), and evidence-based communication. This opinion article proposes a multidimensional framework to strengthen HPV vaccine confidence by: (1) employing prebunking strategies grounded in psychological inoculation theory to build cognitive resistance to misinformation; (2) applying infodemiological modeling for real-time monitoring, predictive analysis, and rapid response; (3) leveraging algorithmic governance to prioritize credible, provaccine content; (4) utilizing AI-driven tools to identify and flag misinformation; and (5) transforming social media into a public health ally. Collectively, these ethically governed, complementary approaches can transform social media from a conduit of misinformation into a powerful catalyst for HPV vaccine confidence and acceptance across the globe.

title: 13 | Secondary prevention of cervical cancer: diagnostic pathways and follow-up in the Local Health Authority of Reggio Calabria
abstract: Cervical cancer is closely associated with persistent infection by human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly high-risk genotypes HPV 16 and 18. Progression from persistent infection to intraepithelial lesion and carcinoma is generally slow, allowing early detection and treatment of high-grade cervical lesions and prevention of invasive disease. Organized screening is therefore essential to reduce incidence and mortality. The current model includes cytology for women aged 25–29 years and primary HPV-DNA testing in older women, followed by cytological triage of HPV-positive women and colposcopy when indicated. Materials and Methods. A descriptive analysis was conducted of the organized cervical cancer screening programme implemented by the Reggio Calabria Local Health Authority in 2025. The programme used HPV-DNA testing through self-sampling, followed, in positive cases, by cytological triage and referral for colposcopy according to GISCi recommendations. The number of invited and participating women, first-level positive results, colposcopic outcomes, diagnoses of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or 3 (CIN2/CIN3), and treatments performed were analysed. The contribution of a mobile screening unit in reaching geographically underserved areas was also assessed.Results. Among 25,059 women in the target population, 8,923 participated in screening; 2,005 invitations were undelivered, resulting in a participation rate of 39%. Overall, 397 women were referred for colposcopy. Of these, 161 received a grade 0 result and continued the scheduled screening pathway, while 227 had a grade 1 result, including 5 CIN2 diagnoses. Nine women were classified as grade 2; among the available data, 4 had negative results, 1 had CIN2, 1 had CIN3, and 1 refused further diagnostic assessment. Seven women underwent treatment. HPV vaccination was recommended to all unvaccinated women. The mobile unit improved access to screening in geographically difficult-to-reach areas.Conclusions. The experience of the Reggio Calabria Local Health Authority supports the value of HPV-based screening with self-sampling, provided that it is integrated with a structured cytological triage pathway, one-year surveillance, and colposcopy for persistent HPV infection or abnormal cytology. The organized programme and mobile unit facilitated the early detection of high-grade lesions and improved accessibility. Continued outcome monitoring, completion of missing data, and establishment of a biobank could support future studies on molecular biomarkers for triage.

Progression from persistent infection to intraepithelial lesion and carcinoma is generally slow, allowing early detection and treatment of high-grade cervical lesions and prevention of invasive disease. Organized screening is therefore essential to reduce incidence and mortality. The current model includes cytology for women aged 25–29 years and primary HPV-DNA testing in older women, followed by cytological triage of HPV-positive women and colposcopy when indicated. Materials and Methods. A descriptive analysis was conducted of the organized cervical cancer screening programme implemented by the Reggio Calabria Local Health Authority in 2025. The programme used HPV-DNA testing through self-sampling, followed, in positive cases, by cytological triage and referral for colposcopy according to GISCi recommendations. The number of invited and participating women, first-level positive results, colposcopic outcomes, diagnoses of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or 3 (CIN2/CIN3), and treatments performed were analysed. The contribution of a mobile screening unit in reaching geographically underserved areas was also assessed.Results. Among 25,059 women in the target population, 8,923 participated in screening; 2,005 invitations were undelivered, resulting in a participation rate of 39%. Overall, 397 women were referred for colposcopy. Of these, 161 received a grade 0 result and continued the scheduled screening pathway, while 227 had a grade 1 result, including 5 CIN2 diagnoses. Nine women were classified as grade 2; among the available data, 4 had negative results, 1 had CIN2, 1 had CIN3, and 1 refused further diagnostic assessment. Seven women underwent treatment. HPV vaccination was recommended to all unvaccinated women. The mobile unit improved access to screening in geographically difficult-to-reach areas.Conclusions. The experience of the Reggio Calabria Local Health Authority supports the value of HPV-based screening with self-sampling, provided that it is integrated with a structured cytological triage pathway, one-year surveillance, and colposcopy for persistent HPV infection or abnormal cytology. The organized programme and mobile unit facilitated the early detection of high-grade lesions and improved accessibility. Continued outcome monitoring, completion of missing data, and establishment of a biobank could support future studies on molecular biomarkers for triage.

title: Patient and public involvement in a cancer prevention research department: lessons learned from the DIADEME group.
abstract: Although public and patient involvement (PPI) is increasingly promoted in health research, its practical implementation remains rarely documented, especially in primary cancer prevention. The DIADEME group, aimed to address this gap through an empirical descriptive and process‐evaluation study reporting how citizens and patients involvement in research, governance, and preventive actions is organised and performed within the Department of Prevention Cancer Environment of a French Comprehensive Cancer Care Center (Centre Léon Bérard, Lyon). Citizens and patients with prior experience in PPI were recruited through associations, partners, flyers, to form a PPI resource group. A group manager coordinated the initiative, and a patient facilitator provided independent feedback on PPI to ensure balanced collaboration. The engagement framework (mission statement, engagement charter, and annual action plan) was co-developed during the first two meetings. PPI was evaluated using the Patient and Public Engagement Evaluation Tool framework and qualitative feedback. Five patients and five citizens were recruited as PPI resource group members, with associations being the most effective recruitment channel. Their contribution to 9 monthly meetings and additional tasks led to tangible outcomes: revisions to a colorectal cancer prevention study to better address patient needs, the development of an educational card game for Human Papillomavirus prevention, and updates of public information sheets on a public information portal. The patient facilitator had a critical role in improving meetings dynamic enabling more time for participant contributions. The PPI evaluation generated practical recommendations to improve group management, communication workflows, and impact tracking. The DIADEME group demonstrates that involving patients and citizens in cancer prevention research and communication activities is both feasible and valuable, though integration into governance remains challenging. This study provides lessons learned on structuring participatory processes that may support other teams and organisations implementing PPI initiatives in cancer prevention and beyond. Patients and members of the public can improve cancer prevention. Their experiential knowledge and understanding of health issues, derived from living with a disease or experience with cancer risk factors and prevention environments, provide valuable insights for research and prevention activities. But many teams still do not explain how they involve people in their team or project. The DIADEME group looked at how patients and citizens took part in a prevention department at a cancer centre in Lyon, France. The aim was to involve them in research, communication, and decisions about prevention in the department. Five patients and five citizens joined a group that worked with the prevention team. Community organisations, partners, and flyers helped us reach them. A group manager guided the work. A patient facilitator supported the group by ensuring and facilitating the participation of all patients and citizens. In the first meetings, the group wrote a shared mission, a charter, and a plan for the year. Over nine months, the group met monthly and took part in several tasks. They improved a study on colorectal cancer prevention based on their experience. They helped create an educational card game about a virus that can cause cancer. They also helped update public information sheets on a national health website. This work showed the feasibility of involving patients and citizens in a cancer prevention department. This is both possible and helpful. It led to many ideas to improve how to plan, communicate, and follow the impact of PPI. This may help other teams and organisations support citizen and patient involvement.

title: Therapeutic HPV vaccines for PD-1 blockade–resistant HPV-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: mechanistic rationale, clinical limitations, and biomarker-guided combinations
abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a common malignancy that continues to present substantial therapeutic challenges despite decades of research. Immune checkpoint blockade agents targeting the programmed death receptor-1 (PD-1) axis have emerged as a frontline therapeutic modality for patients with recurrent/metastatic disease. However, suboptimal objective response rates and pervasive inherent and acquired resistance mechanisms significantly limit clinical efficacy. Notably, the escalating incidence of human papillomavirus (HPV)-driven HNSCC, particularly oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC), has necessitated novel treatment paradigms. The HPV-encoded oncoviral antigens represent optimal targets for precision immunotherapeutic interventions. Here, we summarize the multifactorial mechanisms underlying resistance to PD-1 blockade in HNSCC and discuss how therapeutic HPV vaccines may restore antitumor immune responses by remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) and expanding virus-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes. These findings support the biological rationale for combining therapeutic HPV vaccines with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade; however, this strategy should still be regarded as investigational because clinical benefit has not been consistently demonstrated in randomized studies. In addition, we review recent preclinical and translational advances, compare major vaccine delivery platforms, and discuss future research directions and challenges in this evolving field. Finally, we advance a working hypothesis that therapeutic efficacy is contingent upon three biological prerequisites—intact MHC-I antigen presentation, baseline PD-L1 expression, and the absence of dominant non-PD-1 immunosuppressive barriers—and discuss the implications of this precision-enrichment framework for future trial design.

title: HPV vaccination initiation among preadolescents in Veneto, Italy: associations with chronic conditions and socioeconomic disadvantage
abstract: BACKGROUND: Identifying population groups with lower human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination uptake is essential for developing targeted public health interventions. This study examined whether chronic conditions and sociodemographic factors were associated with HPV vaccination initiation among preadolescents in the Veneto Region of Italy. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using data from Pedianet, an Italian primary-care pediatric database. The study included children born between 2008 and 2011 who were followed between 9 and 12 years of age. Vaccination initiation was defined as receipt of at least one HPV vaccine dose from the ninth birthday to the day before the thirteenth birthday. Associations with sex, birth cohort, selected chronic conditions, disability, income-based healthcare exemption, and pediatric healthcare utilization were assessed using multivariable multilevel logistic regression, with a random intercept for family pediatrician. RESULTS: Among 19,245 children followed by 93 pediatricians, 53.6% received at least one HPV vaccine dose. Asthma was associated with higher odds of vaccination initiation (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.36; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.12-1.67), whereas disability (aOR 0.71; 95% CI 0.58-0.88), income-based healthcare exemption (aOR 0.81; 95% CI 0.76-0.86), and male sex (aOR 0.79; 95% CI 0.74-0.84) were associated with lower odds of initiation. Associations with receipt of two HPV vaccine doses within the same age window were broadly consistent with those for initiation. CONCLUSIONS: HPV vaccination initiation was associated with health-related and sociodemographic factors. Lower uptake among children with administratively recognized disability, those with income-based healthcare exemptions, and boys identifies groups that may benefit from targeted vaccination support. Further research should clarify the barriers underlying these associations.
