title: Ultrasensitive and Specific Detection of Neutralization-Correlated Serum Antibodies Via Secondary Antibody-DNA Linker-Mediated Magnetic Bead-Based Proximity Extension Assay.
abstract: Sensitive, accurate, and readily deployable detection of neutralizing antibody (NAb) titers is essential for evaluating vaccine efficacy and population-level immunity. Here, we report an Antibody-DNA Linker (AND Linker) comprising a fusion of Protein A/G, a G4S flexible peptide, and duck circovirus replication initiator protein (DCV). This design enables orthogonal, site-specific assembly: the N-terminal Protein A/G binds the IgG Fc region, while the C-terminal DCV covalently captures 5' ssDNA at a defined 1:1 molar ratio. Unlike random chemical crosslinking, which suffers from heterogeneous attachment sites, variable stoichiometry, and poor reproducibility, the AND Linker ensures uniform functional orientation and minimal batch-to-batch variation. By optimizing ssDNA secondary structure, we further enhanced DCV recognition efficiency. Integrating this linker into a magnetic bead-based proximity extension assay (termed SADL-MPEA), we achieved femtomolar-level detection of serum antibodies highly correlated with neutralizing activity. For HPV16 and HPV18, SADL-MPEA demonstrated limits of detection (LOD) approximately three orders of magnitude lower than conventional PEA using random chemical conjugation. In clinical serum validation against the pseudovirus neutralization test (PBNT), SADL-MPEA showed strong concordance (Pearson's r = 0.84-0.85), confirming its utility as a reliable surrogate for functional neutralization capacity. Diagnostic performance was exceptional, with sensitivities of 90.9% (HPV16) and 83.3% (HPV18), 100% specificity for both, and an area under the ROC curve of 0.99. Crucially, SADL-MPEA requires only antigen-coated magnetic beads to adapt to new targets, as the DNA-labeled secondary antibody remains universal. This platform offers a simple, high-throughput, and scalable solution for NAb-correlated antibody detection in research and clinical settings.

title: Men get STIs, women get cancer: The representation of the HPV vaccine in public health communication on Vietnamese Facebook
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a highly prevalent sexually transmitted infection (STI) that can be transmitted by individuals of any sex to partners of the same or different sex. The HPV vaccine, introduced in 2006, can protect people of all genders against HPV-associated cancers and genital warts, yet public health campaigns promoting the vaccine have predominantly targeted women and parents of young girls for cervical cancer prevention. This focus leaves men and men who have sex with men (MSM) underinformed, despite MSM being at higher risk of HPV-related cancer. Using the extended parallel process model (EPPM), this study examines the communication landscape surrounding the HPV vaccine in Vietnam following the Ministry of Health’s 2024 decision to expand the vaccine recommendation to include both males and females aged 9–45 years. The content analysis of 479 public Facebook posts reveals that a significant portion of posts target adult women, while men and sexual minorities are less frequently addressed. Consistent with earlier literature, the findings in this study indicate a persistent feminization of HPV discourse, in which messaging often emphasizes cervical cancer prevention. Gendered narratives also portray men as more susceptible to STIs, and women as more vulnerable to cancer. As a result, according to the EPPM, the group most likely to seek vaccination is adult women. Further, the study finds that the HPV vaccine is consistently framed using heteronormative and neoliberal lenses, as well as the use of ‘algospeak’ to circumvent content moderation of stigmatized topics such as STIs. These findings highlight the tension between inclusive health policies and the gendered realities of public health messaging. By revealing the persistent focus on women and the relative neglect of men and sexual minorities in HPV vaccine communication, this study underscores the need for more inclusive communication strategies to promote vaccine take-up among all eligible populations.

HPV16/18 was independently associated with CIN2+ (adjusted OR 10.67, 95% CI 4.94 to 23.05, versus women negative for all 14 high-risk types), whereas no statistically significant association was detected for the commonest type, HPV52 (genotype-specific adjusted OR 1.23, 0.72 to 2.13). Absolute CIN2+ risk per genotype-positive woman was 18.9% to 32.9% for HPV16 and 9.1% to 18.7% for HPV58, against 4.3% to 10.2% for HPV52, and this ranking was unchanged across a sensitivity analysis of the verification-bias correction. In this hospital-based population the commonest genotype was not the one most strongly associated with prevalent CIN2+, and HPV prevalence did not fall with age. Genotype-specific risk stratification and the upper age limit for screening warrant evaluation in prospective, population-based studies.

title: Cervical Cancer Knowledge, Misconceptions, and Educational Needs Among Women Undergoing Screening in Dodoma, Tanzania: A Mixed-Methods Study.
abstract: Cervical cancer prevention depends on women understanding that the disease is preventable and that screening is needed before symptoms develop. This study assessed cervical cancer knowledge and explored misconceptions, information sources, and educational needs among women undergoing screening at Dodoma Regional Referral Hospital, Tanzania. A concurrent mixed-methods study was conducted from January to March 2026. Quantitative data were collected from 422 women aged 25 years or older using a 25-item Cervical Cancer Awareness Measure-based composite incorporating 20 knowledge/awareness responses and five information-source indicators; 20 purposively selected women completed in-depth interviews. Composite scores were categorized as poor (0-14), moderate (15-19), or good (20-25). Quantitative data were summarized descriptively, qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and findings were integrated during interpretation. Overall, 211 (50.0%) participants were classified as poor, 184 (43.6%) as moderate, and 27 (6.4%) as good on the composite. Only 24.4% recognized that cervical cancer was preventable, 42.4% had heard of human papillomavirus vaccination, and 21.6% recognized the role of regular screening in early detection. Health workers were the most frequently reported information source (48.8%). Interviews revealed superficial awareness, misconceptions about causation, fear of severe illness and death, and a strong desire for education. These findings identify priority messages for culturally appropriate education at screening encounters and in community settings; effectiveness of such education requires prospective evaluation.
journal: Journal of cancer education : the official journal of the American Association for Cancer Education

title: Multilevel Barriers and Facilitators to Cervical Cancer Screening Among Trans Masculine People: A Narrative Review
abstract: Purpose: This narrative review synthesized empirical evidence on barriers and facilitators to cervical cancer screening among trans masculine people. Methods: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched through February 7, 2026, for English-language empirical studies published from January 1, 2015. Findings were organized using a socioecological framework and interpreted through the Gender Minority Stress and Resilience model. Results: Nineteen studies from eight countries met the inclusion criteria. Individual barriers included procedure-triggered gender dysphoria, pain, trauma activation, low perceived risk, and limited sexual health literacy. Interpersonal barriers included misgendering, non-preferred anatomical terminology, provider unfamiliarity, gatekeeping, and anticipated discrimination. Institutional barriers included the framing of screening as women’s health, non-inclusive materials, loss of invitations or coverage after a gender-marker change, and cost. Facilitators included self-sampling for high-risk human papillomavirus testing, gender-affirming therapeutic relationships, trauma-informed care, inclusive environments, peer support, and invitation systems independent of the gender marker. Conclusions: The reviewed studies identified interacting barriers across the screening pathway. Self-sampling was acceptable to many participants and was described as reducing procedural burden, but preferences varied and relational and institutional barriers persisted. The findings supported offering modality choice alongside gender-affirming, trauma-informed care, and anatomy-based eligibility; evidence of intervention effectiveness remained limited.

title: Construction of a nomogram for predicting pathological upgrading after LEEP in patients with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 based on colposcopic morphological features: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) grade 1/2 diagnosed by colposcopy-directed biopsy may underestimate the final lesion grade found on excision. In patients who proceed to Loop Electrosurgical Excision Procedure (LEEP), postoperative pathology may show histopathological upgrading relative to the preoperative biopsy. Although HPV testing and ThinPrep Cytology Test (TCT) are standard screening tools, their differential value in this LEEP-selected CIN1/2 population remains unclear. This study aimed to identify factors associated with pathological upgrading after LEEP and to construct an internally validated nomogram based on colposcopic morphological features. We retrospectively analyzed 122 patients who underwent LEEP for clinical indications between 2020 and 2025 with preoperative biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2. Pathological upgrading was defined as biopsy CIN1 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN2, or biopsy CIN2 with LEEP pathology ≥ CIN3 (invasive carcinoma included). These 2 transitions were prespecified and are clinically distinct; event counts were, therefore, also reported by baseline biopsy grade. Multivariable logistic regression was used to develop a nomogram. Discrimination and calibration were assessed with ROC analysis and bootstrap internal validation; clinical utility was explored with decision curve analysis (DCA). Pathological upgrading occurred in 46/122 (37.7%) patients in this LEEP-selected cohort, including 4/15 (26.7%) with baseline CIN1 and 42/107 (39.3%) with baseline CIN2. In the multivariable model, Reid Colposcopic Index (OR = 1.41, P = .013) and number of involved quadrants (OR = 1.93, P = .018) were significantly associated with upgrading, whereas menopausal status (OR = 2.83, P = .059) and biopsy count (OR = 0.70, P = .068) did not reach conventional significance but were retained as candidate predictors. HPV genotype category and TCT were not significantly associated with upgrading. The nomogram showed apparent AUC 0.801 (95% CI 0.719-0.883) on internal evaluation; calibration and DCA supported exploratory clinical utility within this surgical cohort. In women with biopsy-confirmed CIN1/2 who already had indications for LEEP, colposcopic morphological features (Reid score and lesion extent) were more informative than HPV/TCT for predicting histopathological upgrading after excision. The nomogram may assist risk stratification within this selected surgical population. An ROC-derived probability threshold of 43% is presented only as an exploratory cut-point requiring external validation and should not yet be used as a standalone rule to choose observation vs LEEP in unselected CIN1/2 patients.

title: Cytology of HPV-Independent Cervical Carcinomas: Morphologic Spectrum, Clinical Correlates, and Ancillary Testing
abstract: Cervical cancer is one of the most common cancers that can be diagnosed by cytologic features. While the past focus was mostly on human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated cervical carcinomas, the studies on HPV-independent cervical carcinomas have become more extensive with the advancement in ancillary tests, including molecular tests. The development of digital pathology also provides additional opportunities for more accurate cytologic diagnosis. We would like to summarise the current knowledge on the epidemiology, cytomorphology, and ancillary studies for different types of HPV-independent cervical carcinomas, and explore the use of digital pathology in the diagnosis of HPV-independent cervical carcinomas. Case reports, case series, and research articles are identified on PubMed using keywords “HPV-independent”, “cervical carcinomas”, “digital pathology”, and the specific names of subtypes of HPV-independent cervical carcinomas. The studies are selected based on their relevance to cytology, with an emphasis on new updates of ancillary tests. HPV-independent cervical carcinomas are classified based on the histological features, with distinct cytomorphological, immunocytochemical, and molecular features for each subtype. The prognosis is generally worse than HPV-associated cervical carcinomas. Accurate diagnosis is limited by a small number of cases and limited exposure among cytotechnicians and cytopathologists. The use of digital pathology can potentially improve diagnostic accuracy, while more studies are required before the adoption of digital pathology for the diagnosis of HPV-independent cervical carcinomas. Recognition of suspicious clinical features, liberal use of immunocytochemistry, and molecular testing are essential to accurate cytologic diagnosis of HPV-independent cervical carcinomas.

title: Epigenetic Silencing of Tumor Suppressor Genes through Promoter Hypermethylation in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: From Molecular Insights to Clinical Applications
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) continues to be a devastating disease, largely because it is often detected too late and tends to resist conventional therapies. Collectively, promoter hypermethylation of tumor suppressor genes represents an early, reversible, and clinically actionable event in OSCC. Emerging methylation-based biomarkers, particularly salivary gene panels, demonstrate promise for non-invasive early detection and longitudinal monitoring. Furthermore, the reversibility of epigenetic silencing provides a rationale for epigenetic therapies, including DNMT (DNA methyltransferase) inhibitors in combination with immunotherapy. Although most evidence remains exploratory and often extrapolated from broader head and neck cancer cohorts, these molecular insights lay the groundwork for future OSCC-specific diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.HPV-specific methylation thresholds, such as CDKN2A (Cyclin Dependent Kinase Inhibitor 2A) in HPV-negative cancers—where OSCC-specific thresholds are limited and most data are derived from OPSCC (Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma)—and RASSF1A (Ras Association Domain Family Member 1A) in HPV-positive cancers—primarily based on OPSCC rather than OSCC—improve diagnostic and prognostic precision. New non-invasive approaches for early detection and monitoring, such as saliva-based methylation testing HOXA9/NID2 panels (HomeoboxA9), are also highlighted. This review summarizes new evidence that promoter hypermethylation causes oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) by abnormally silencing tumor suppressor genes. We also examine the molecular basis of this phenomenon, stressing how tobacco exposure and HPV infection affect these cancers' methylation landscapes. We believe that incorporating these epigenetic indicators into clinical practice may improve OSCC management.
journal: Journal of Health Science and Medical Research

title: Risk-Based Triage of Women with Persistent HR-HPV Positivity at 12-Month Recall in Cervical Cancer Screening: A Multicenter Retrospective Evaluation of Cytology and Partial HPV Genotyping
abstract: Background: Under the current Italian HPV-based cervical screening protocol, women with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) positivity at the 12-month recall are referred to colposcopy regardless of cytology results. Although this strategy maximizes lesion detection, it may result in a high number of colposcopies, most of which do not identify CIN2+. We evaluated whether partial HPV genotyping combined with cytology can improve risk stratification in women with persistent HPV positivity at the 12-month recall. Methods: A multicenter retrospective analysis of cervical screening data collected from four Italian screening programs (Florence, Padua, Umbria and Emilia Romagna) was performed. Among the 270,714 women screened between 2015 and 2019 (2016–2018 in Florence), 4589 women with persistent HR-HPV positivity at 12-month recall after baseline HPV-positive/NILM (negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy) results were included. Four alternative triage strategies based on cytology and HPV 16/18 genotyping were retrospectively simulated and compared with the current protocol. Outcomes included CIN2 (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2) or worse (CIN2+) detection, relative sensitivity for CIN2+ and CIN3 (cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 3) or worse (CIN3+), positive predictive value (PPV) and reduction in colposcopy referrals. Results: Under the current protocol, 4589 colposcopies identified 327 CIN2+ lesions, including 113 CIN3+ lesions, yielding a PPV for CIN2+ of 7.1%. Overall, 36.7% of CIN2+ lesions were associated with NILM cytology at recall. HPV 16/18 genotyping identified 43.3% of these cytologically occult lesions. In this retrospective simulation, among the evaluated strategies, referral of HPV 16/18-positive women regardless of cytology and referral of women with low-grade or worse cytology regardless of genotype would have achieved the most favorable balance between sensitivity and efficiency. This approach would have reduced colposcopy referrals by 57.7% (95% CI, 56.3–59.2), nearly doubled the PPV for CIN2+ to 13.4% (95% CI, 11.9–14.9) and maintained relative sensitivities of 79.2% (95% CI, 74.5–83.3) for CIN2+ and 85.0% (95% CI, 77.2–90.4) for CIN3+. Performance varied across centers, with imprecise center-specific estimates (relative CIN3+ sensitivity of Strategy 2 from 62.5% in Emilia Romagna to 91.1% in Umbria), so generalizability should be assessed cautiously. Conclusions: Combining partial HPV genotyping with cytology would have substantially improved risk stratification in women with persistent HR-HPV positivity at 12-month recall. In this retrospective simulation, a risk-based approach would have substantially reduced immediate colposcopies while maintaining a relative sensitivity for CIN3+ of 85.0%. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support prospective evaluation of integrating molecular and cytological information into 12-month recall management.
authors: ISPRO Cervical Cancer Screening Working Group

title: Knowledge And Practice Of Cervical Cancer Screening Among Women In Ibadan, Oyo State
abstract: Cervical cancer is a major public health concern, particularly in developing countries where awareness and utilization of preventive services are still limited.This study assessed the knowledge, awareness, and preventive practices related to cervical cancer, Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination, and Pap smear screening among respondents.A descriptive survey research design was adopted, and data were collected from 537 respondents using a structured questionnaire.The findings revealed that a large proportion of respondents were aware of cervical cancer and understood that Pap smear tests can detect the disease at an early stage.Similarly, a considerable number were aware of the HPV vaccine as a preventive measure.However, the uptake of both HPV vaccination and Pap smear screening was relatively low.Among respondents with daughters, only a small percentage reported that their daughters had received the HPV vaccine.Major barriers to vaccination and screening included concerns about side effects, cost, fear of the screening procedure, lack of adequate information, and cultural or religious beliefs.Despite these challenges, many respondents expressed willingness to recommend HPV vaccination and Pap smear screening to others.The study concludes that although awareness of cervical cancer prevention exists, there remains a significant gap between knowledge and the actual utilization of preventive services.The study therefore recommends intensified public health education, subsidized vaccination and screening programs, and the integration of cervical cancer screening into routine healthcare services to improve prevention and early detection.

title: Viral infections and the risk of prostate cancer: a two-sample Mendelian randomization study with multi-cohort replication and an extended viral antibody panel
abstract: Observational evidence linking viral infection to prostate cancer (PCa) remains controversial. We evaluated the potential causal relationships between serological markers of viral infection and PCa risk using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR). PCa summary statistics came from PRACTICAL (79,148 cases, 61,106 controls), FinnGen R10 (15,199/131,266) and the Wang 2023 European-ancestry subset (122,188/604,640). Inverse-variance-weighted estimation was primary, with extensive sensitivity analyses (MR-Egger, weighted-median, MR-PRESSO, Steiger directionality testing, colocalization, multivariable, reverse and mediation MR) and cross-cohort meta-analysis. An extended 37-trait serological panel covering 12 viruses was additionally screened. EBV EBNA-1 antibody levels were associated with increased PCa risk in PRACTICAL (OR = 1.069, P = 0.032) and replicated in FinnGen (OR = 1.117, P = 0.017) and Wang 2023 (OR = 1.062, P = 0.036), with a cross-cohort random-effects meta-analytic OR of 1.074 (95% CI 1.034–1.115, P = 2.1 × 10-4, I2 = 0%), and in the fully independent PRACTICAL + FinnGen meta-analysis (OR = 1.084, P = 0.002). The association was independent of CMV pp150 in multivariable MR, free of reverse causality and directional pleiotropy, and Steiger-confirmed. CMV pp150 showed directionally consistent, meta-analytically significant effects (OR = 1.038, P = 0.020). The extended panel identified two novel Bonferroni-significant, cross-cohort-replicated associations: Merkel cell polyomavirus seropositivity with reduced risk (meta OR = 0.967, P = 1.6 × 10-5) and BK polyomavirus seropositivity with increased risk (meta OR = 1.267, P = 1.0 × 10-5). Genetically proxied EBV latent infection is a candidate causal factor for PCa, and MCV (protective) and BK polyomavirus (risk) seropositivity are novel candidates warranting mechanistic and multi-ancestry validation. Effect sizes are small and, under Bonferroni correction for 37 traits, only the polyomavirus signals survive; all findings should therefore be regarded as hypothesis-generating pending further independent replication.

title: Narrative and Linguistic Strategies in HPV Vaccine Communication: A Content Analysis of Government, Medical Institutions, and Practitioners’ Accounts on Sina Weibo
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a central public health concern in China, and public engagement with HPV-related content on social media varies widely. Identifying which narrative and linguistic strategies elicit stronger responses is therefore essential for improving the effectiveness of vaccine communication. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, an approach that identifies which combinations of message features are associated with an outcome, this study examines how narrative presence, narrative perspective, grammatical mood, linguistic modality, and account type combine to correspond to engagement with 638 HPV vaccine posts on Sina Weibo. The analysis identifies several distinct configurations associated with high audience engagement, as well as multiple patterns linked to low engagement. Posts from medical institutions were associated with stronger engagement when they adopted second-person, third-person, or impersonal narrative forms with high-modality language (i.e., language with high certainty), while medical practitioners were associated with high engagement when they relied on question-only posts that encouraged a conversational orientation. Low engagement was most often observed in non-narrative declarative posts using medium-modality language (i.e., moderately assertive wording) from medical practitioners, while tentative, low-modality language characterized three of the five low-engagement configurations and none of the high-engagement configurations. These findings specify boundary conditions under which narrative and linguistic strategies are associated with audience engagement, and illustrate how grammatical mood and linguistic modality function in relation to message content and source type. Moreover, the results offer practical insights for designing more engaging HPV vaccine communication on social media.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study focuses on the narrative and linguistic strategies used in HPV vaccine communication on Sina Weibo, examining how these strategies influence audience engagement. The central question is how different combinations of message features, such as narrative presence, perspective, grammatical mood, and linguistic modality, relate to engagement levels with HPV vaccine posts.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review employs a narrative content analysis approach, using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis to identify configurations of message features associated with engagement. The study analyzed 638 HPV vaccine posts from government, medical institutions, and practitioners on Sina Weibo, focusing on narrative forms, linguistic modality, and account type.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The analysis found that posts from medical institutions using second-person, third-person, or impersonal narrative forms with high-modality language (i.e., language with high certainty) were associated with stronger audience engagement. Additionally, medical practitioners' posts that encouraged a conversational orientation through question-only formats also showed high engagement. In contrast, non-narrative declarative posts with medium-modality language from medical practitioners were linked to low engagement.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study highlights that tentative, low-modality language was characteristic of three of the five low-engagement configurations, indicating a potential gap in understanding how different linguistic styles affect engagement. The findings also suggest that the effectiveness of narrative and linguistic strategies may depend on the source type and message content, but the exact mechanisms remain underexplored.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The results provide practical insights for designing more engaging HPV vaccine communication on social media. They emphasize the importance of using high-modality language and appropriate narrative forms when disseminating information from medical institutions, while also suggesting that conversational formats may be effective for practitioners. These findings can inform future strategies for improving public health messaging related to HPV vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores how narrative and linguistic strategies in HPV vaccine communication on Sina Weibo influence audience engagement. Using fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis, the study identifies configurations of message features, such as narrative form and linguistic modality, that correlate with high or low engagement. Posts from medical institutions using high-modality language and various narrative forms showed stronger engagement, while non-narrative declarative posts with medium-modality language were associated with lower engagement. The findings suggest that message design should consider both the source type and the linguistic style to enhance vaccine communication effectiveness. The study also highlights gaps in understanding the precise mechanisms behind engagement differences and offers actionable insights for improving public health messaging.

elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论采用叙述性内容分析方法,使用模糊集定性比较分析来识别与参与度相关的消息特征的配置。该研究分析了新浪微博上来自政府、医疗机构和从业人员的 638 条 HPV 疫苗 帖子,重点关注叙事形式、语言模式和账户类型。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果为在社交媒体上设计更具吸引力的 HPV 疫苗 通信提供了实用的见解。他们强调在传播医疗机构信息时使用高模态语言和适当的叙述形式的重要性,同时也表明对话形式可能对从业者有效。这些发现可以为未来改善与 HPV 疫苗 相关的公共卫生信息传递的策略提供信息。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究重点关注 HPV 疫苗 在新浪微博上的交流中使用的叙事和语言策略,研究这些策略如何影响受众参与度。核心问题是消息特征的不同组合,例如叙述存在、视角、语法情绪和语言模式,如何与 HPV 疫苗 帖子的参与度相关。

title: HPV-mediated OPSCC in minority nationalities region along the border of South China: a multi-center study
abstract: Abstract Background In recent years, the incidence of HPV-mediated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) has shown an increasing trend. Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region is a border region with ethnic minorities, and current research on HPV-mediated OPSCC still remains a gap. Therefore, HPV-mediated OPSCC cases and their HPV infection sub-types were detected in this retrospective and multi-center study, aiming to explore the incidence situation of HPV-mediated OPSCC in minority nationalities region along the border of South China. Methods A total of 361 cases of OPSCC specimens collected from nine hospitals in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region from 2005–2023 were analyzed using a combined detection method incorporating p16 immunohistochemistry (IHC), RNAscope HPV HR18 in situ hybridization (ISH) and gene chip technology to identify HPV-mediated OPSCC cases and their HPV sub-types. Differences in characteristics between HPV-mediated and non-HPV-mediated OPSCC were assessed using the chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test, and survival analyses were performed using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test. Independent prognostic factors were evaluated by Cox regression to derive hazard ratios (HRs), with patients alive at last follow-up or lost to follow-up censored in the overall survival (OS) analysis. Results HPV-mediated OPSCC accounted for 12.7% (46/361) of all the OPSCC cases. Among the 46 HPV-mediated OPSCC cases, HPV-16, 18, 33, 52 and 58 were detected in 42 cases. HPV-16 infection rate was the highest among the 5 sub-types, accounting for 92.8% (39/42). Single HPV sub-type infection was observed in 97.6% (41/42) of cases. The proportion of Zhuang and other minority ethnic patients with HPV- mediated OPSCC was higher than that of patients with non- HPV-mediated OPSCC, but the difference was not significant ( P = 0.06). T-stage, recurrence status and surgical intervention were factors influencing overall survival (OS) in patients with HPV-mediated OPSCC. Conclusion HPV-mediated OPSCC cases in minority nationalities region along the border of South China account for approximately 13%. HPV-16 is the predominant sub-type and single sub-type infection is the main infection pattern of HPV-mediated OPSCC in this area.

title: A large-scale cross-sectional cervical screening study reveals HPV prevalence in western China
abstract: Abstract Numerous epidemiological studies have shown that significant regional variations exist in the prevalence of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection and the distribution of HPV subtypes during cervical screening. It is particularly noteworthy that in regions with high-risk factors such as high fertility rates, early pregnancy, and early marriage, women may be at higher risk of HPV infection. Therefore, conducting large-scale studies on cervical screening—especially in these underserved areas—is of great significance. This study conducted a large-scale cross-sectional study on cervical screening in western China (Xichang, Sichuan) using a combination of thin-layer cytology (TCT) and HPV testing. Among the 3,522 women who met the inclusion criteria, 13.77% exhibited cervical or vaginal abnormalities (positive cytology or HPV test results). Colposcopy revealed a total of 58 cases of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and cervical cancer. Among the participants who underwent HPV testing as part of cervical screening, 112 (23.09%) were infected with HPV; of these, 20 (17.86%) were infected with HPV types 16/18, while 82.14% were infected with non-HPV 16/18 types. Contraceptive method, number of pregnancies, and number of deliveries had a significant impact on the risk of HPV infection. HPV infection, particularly infection with high-risk HPV types, was positively correlated with the progression of cervical CIN lesions. The results of this study provide an empirical basis for understanding the epidemiology of HPV in Yanyuan County, Xichang City, China.

title: Development and psychometric evaluation of a modified persian HPV-related quality of life (HPV-QoL) questionnaire
abstract: Abstract Background Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection can substantially affect quality of life. Although the HPV-QoL measures this impact, no validated Persian version has been available. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of a modified 12-item Persian version derived from the original HPV-QoL (HPV-QoL) questionnaire among individuals with HPV infection or anogenital warts, providing nurses and midwives with a reliable tool for assessing HPV-related quality of life. Methodology A cross-sectional study (September 2023–November 2024) was conducted to translate the HPV-QoL and assess its psychometric properties among 450 participants with HPV positivity or anogenital warts. Validity assessment included face validity (10 participants), content validity (15 experts), and construct validity using exploratory (200 participants) and confirmatory factor analyses (200 participants). Reliability (30 participants) was examined through internal consistency, test–retest stability, and absolute reliability, alongside measurement error, responsiveness, and interpretability. Results The Modified Persian HPV-QoL showed a unidimensional structure consisting of 12 items that together explained 63.31% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the adequacy of the model fit (CFI = 0.983; RMSEA = 0.06; CI: 0.018–0.084). Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α = 0.972). Test–retest reliability was also excellent (ICC = 0.978). Preliminary distribution-based indices related to responsiveness and interpretability were reported acceptability. Conclusion The modified 12-item Persian HPV-related quality of life questionnaire demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties in Iranian adults with HPV infection or anogenital warts. Because its structure differs from the original HPV-QoL, scores should not be interpreted as directly comparable with those of the original instrument.

source_records.title: Development and psychometric evaluation of a modified persian HPV-related quality of life (HPV-QoL) questionnaire
source_records.abstract: Abstract Background Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection can substantially affect quality of life. Although the HPV-QoL measures this impact, no validated Persian version has been available. This study aimed to translate, culturally adapt, and evaluate the psychometric properties of a modified 12-item Persian version derived from the original HPV-QoL (HPV-QoL) questionnaire among individuals with HPV infection or anogenital warts, providing nurses and midwives with a reliable tool for assessing HPV-related quality of life. Methodology A cross-sectional study (September 2023–November 2024) was conducted to translate the HPV-QoL and assess its psychometric properties among 450 participants with HPV positivity or anogenital warts. Validity assessment included face validity (10 participants), content validity (15 experts), and construct validity using exploratory (200 participants) and confirmatory factor analyses (200 participants). Reliability (30 participants) was examined through internal consistency, test–retest stability, and absolute reliability, alongside measurement error, responsiveness, and interpretability. Results The Modified Persian HPV-QoL showed a unidimensional structure consisting of 12 items that together explained 63.31% of the total variance. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the adequacy of the model fit (CFI = 0.983; RMSEA = 0.06; CI: 0.018–0.084). Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α = 0.972). Test–retest reliability was also excellent (ICC = 0.978). Preliminary distribution-based indices related to responsiveness and interpretability were reported acceptability. Conclusion The modified 12-item Persian HPV-related quality of life questionnaire demonstrated satisfactory psychometric properties in Iranian adults with HPV infection or anogenital warts. Because its structure differs from the original HPV-QoL, scores should not be interpreted as directly comparable with those of the original instrument.

title: Lymphocytes in the tumour immune microenvironment of penile cancer and lymphocyte-modulating therapies: a scoping review
abstract: Penile carcinoma is rare worldwide but a public health problem in parts of Latin America. A meta-analysis estimated a global age-standardised incidence of 0.84 per 100,000 person-years, with the highest continental rate in Latin America (1.40) [1]. In Maranhão, Northeast Brazil, the age-adjusted incidence reached 6.15 per 100,000 in 2004–2014, among the highest reported globally [2]. About half of penile carcinomas carry human papillomavirus (HPV) DNA (pooled prevalence 50.8%, 52 studies, 4,199 cases) [3]. HPV status shapes the tumour immune microenvironment, and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes, regulatory T cells and immune checkpoints such as PD-L1 have been studied as prognostic markers [4,5]. Advanced disease has few effective options: in an international cohort of 92 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors, the objective response rate was 13% and median overall survival 9.8 months [6]. Adoptive cell strategies are at an earlier stage, with tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes successfully expanded from penile cancer specimens [7]. The evidence on lymphocytes in penile cancer is scattered across immunohistochemistry studies, translational and preclinical work, observational cohorts and early-phase trials, with heterogeneous methods and outcomes. Existing syntheses each cover one slice: systematic reviews and meta-analyses of immune checkpoint inhibitor efficacy [15–17], meta-analyses of the prognostic value of PD-L1 [18,19], a scoping review of circulating biomarkers for nodal metastasis [20], and an integrative review of 21 studies (2020–2026) comparing the immune microenvironment of HPV-driven and HPV-independent tumours, posted as a preprint [21]. A search of the records retrieved for this review (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, LILACS) and of the web, OSF and PROSPERO on 3 November 2026 found no scoping review or registered protocol that maps the whole body of evidence on lymphocytes, immune checkpoints and lymphocyte-modulating therapies in penile carcinoma across all study designs, years, preclinical models and registered trials. A scoping review is therefore suited to map what has been studied, how, and where the gaps lie.
authors: Ana Paula Silva de Azevedo dos Santos

title: Programming CRISPR Compartmentalization on DNA Origami for Multiplexed Biosensing.
abstract: CRISPR-Cas12a has emerged as a transformative tool for nucleic acid detection and molecular diagnostics. However, achieving one-pot, orthogonal, multiplexed sensing remains challenging due to the nonspecific trans-cleavage activity of Cas12a. Here, we present a modular DNA origami-based platform that spatially confines and independently controls Cas12a activity, enabling simultaneous detection of multiple DNA targets within a single reaction. This spatial programming approach enables orthogonal one-pot detection of three DNA targets (EGFR L858R/Del19 mutations and HPV16) with minimal cross-talk, demonstrating 60% cleavage efficiency within 120 min at 100 nM. Through integrated molecular dynamics simulations and experimental validation, we identify an optimal ∼6 nm spatial window that maximizes cleavage efficiency, while the platform maintains robust performance in complex biological environments with a 10 nM detection limit in 20% serum. This compartmentalization strategy establishes a framework for spatially programming multi-enzyme systems on DNA nanostructures for synthetic biological circuits.

title: Role of cancer-associated fibroblasts in the progression of cervical cancer and its precancerous lesions: from phenotypic heterogeneity to epithelial-stromal positive feedback loops
abstract: Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HR-HPV) drives most cervical cancers, but only a minority of infected individuals develop invasive disease. This disparity suggests that host and tissue factors, including the local microenvironment, may influence progression. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are a prominent stromal population in cervical cancer, but their timing of activation, phenotypic diversity, and interactions with HPV-infected epithelium remain incompletely understood. This review summarizes reported CAF phenotypes and proposed cellular origins in cervical cancer and its precursor lesions. It evaluates evidence for epithelial–stromal signaling involving transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), exosomal Wnt2B, and interleukin-6 (IL-6), as well as downstream CAF functions. Cross-sectional tissue and single-cell studies suggest that stromal fibroblast states differ between cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CIN) and invasive cervical cancer. These studies do not establish lineage relationships or show that fibroblast changes cause disease progression. We therefore propose a testable positive-feedback model of epithelial–stromal interactions, distinguishing cervical cancer-specific findings from mechanisms inferred from other tumors. Longitudinal sampling and cell-specific perturbation studies are needed to test this model and assess the clinical relevance of CAF-associated markers in precancerous lesions.

title: An in-depth investigation into the role of NO factor in the dynamic immune microenvironment of cervical cancer
abstract: Nitric oxide (NO) exhibits a concentration-dependent dual role within the microenvironment of cervical cancer. This review provides a systematic exploration of the multifaceted regulatory mechanisms of NO in HPV-associated cervical cancer. The E6 and E7 oncoproteins of high-risk HPV notably enhance the expression of inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS/NOS2) through various mechanisms, including epigenetic modifications (such as DNMT3B-mediated hypermethylation of the NOSIP promoter and H3K27ac-enhanced iNOS transcription), post-transcriptional modifications, and metabolic reprogramming (involving pathways such as hypoxia/HIF-1α and lactate/LDHA-YAP). NO is primarily produced by tumor cells, M2-type tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), endothelial cells, and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), resulting in a spatially heterogeneous concentration gradient. At low concentrations (50–200 nM), NO facilitates angiogenesis, promotes immune evasion, enhances the function of regulatory T cells (Tregs) via the IDO1-Kyn-AhR pathway, and drives TAMs towards M2 polarization. Conversely, at high concentrations (> 500 nM), NO induces DNA nitrosative damage (e.g., 8-nitroguanine) and inhibits mitochondrial respiration in T cells, thereby diminishing their cytotoxic efficacy.HPV further contributes to T cell dysfunction by synergistically upregulating inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and arginase, leading to the depletion of arginine within the microenvironment. Emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at the nitric oxide (NO) pathway include the use of iNOS inhibitors, such as 1400 W, in combination with programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) antibodies, dual-targeting NOS/COX-2 inhibitors, as well as HPV-specific nanocarriers, engineered Lactobacillus, and advanced vaginal rings that enable real-time monitoring of NO concentration for precise therapeutic delivery.

title: Cervical Cancer Awareness and Screening Attitudes Among Women Attending a Tertiary Care Hospital in Dhaka, Bangladesh
abstract: BackgroundCervical cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related morbidity and mortality among women worldwide, particularly in low-and middle-income countries.Although cervical cancer can be prevented through early detection and treatment of precancerous lesions, inadequate awareness and unfavourable attitudes towards screening continue to hinder effective prevention efforts. ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess cervical cancer awareness and screening attitude among women attending the Gynaecology Outpatient Department of a tertiary care hospital. MethodsA hospital-based cross-sectional study included 346 women aged 30-60 years attending the Gynaecology Outpatient Department of Dhaka Medical College Hospital.Sociodemographic characteristics and whether participants had heard of cervical cancer were assessed among all 346 women.Detailed cervical cancer awareness and screening-attitude analyses were restricted to the 303 respondents (87.6%) who had heard of cervical cancer.Data were collected through face-to-face interviews using a pretested semi-structured questionnaire.Associations between the four-category awareness outcome and categorical sociodemographic variables were examined using the Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test.Associations involving the binary screening-attitude outcome were examined using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate.Continuous age and monthly income were compared between attitude groups using independent-samples Welch t-tests.All tests were two-sided, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. ResultsThe mean age of the 346 participants was 38.3 ± 6.3 years.Overall, 303 of 346 women (87.6%) had heard of cervical cancer.Among these 303 women, 129 (42.6%) identified unusual vaginal bleeding as a symptom, 86 (28.4%) identified human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as a risk factor, 100 (33.0%) were aware of precancerous cervical lesions, and 216 (71.3%) knew that cervical cancer could be detected through screening.Poor awareness of symptoms and risk factors was observed in 174 (57.4%) and 173 (57.1%), respectively.Sufficient screening attitudes were observed in 86 (28.4%) women, whereas 217 (71.6%) had insufficient attitudes.Age was associated with awareness level (Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test, p = 0.048), whereas occupation was not (p = 0.295).No sociodemographic characteristic was significantly associated with the screening-attitude category. ConclusionsAlthough most respondents had heard of cervical cancer, important gaps remained in their awareness of risk factors, screening methods, HPV infection, and precancerous lesions.Attitudes towards cervical cancer screening were also classified as insufficient in most respondents.

title: Carga de la enfermedad asociada al virus de papiloma humano en mujeres adultas: revisión sistemática
abstract: Introducción: La infección por el virus del papiloma humano (HPV) constituye un problema de salud pública por su elevada frecuencia y asociación con lesiones precancerosas y neoplasias. Su impacto epidemiológico, clínico y económico presenta variaciones poblacionales y geográficas que requieren un análisis integral. Objetivo: Sintetizar la evidencia sobre la carga epidemiológica, clínica y económica del HPV en mujeres adultas, considerando su frecuencia, distribución genotípica, manifestaciones clínicas y variaciones poblacionales y geográficas. Materiales y métodos: Se realizó una revisión sistemática conforme a PRISMA 2020, registrada en PROSPERO con el código CRD420261406577. Se consultaron PubMed, Scopus, SciELO y ScienceDirect para identificar estudios publicados entre 2010 y 2025. Se incluyeron estudios observacionales y poblacionales con indicadores epidemiológicos, clínicos o económicos del HPV en mujeres adultas. La calidad metodológica y el riesgo de sesgo se evaluaron mediante herramientas JBI, adaptadas para estudios ecológicos y poblacionales basados en datos secundarios. Resultados: Se incluyeron 442 publicaciones, con predominio de estudios de prevalencia y transversales descriptivos, poblaciones generales o de cribado y localización cervical. La prevalencia fue el indicador más frecuente, seguida de la incidencia y la persistencia. Predominaron los genotipos HPV16 y HPV18. Las manifestaciones clínicas incluyeron alteraciones citológicas, lesiones intraepiteliales y neoplasias. La carga económica presentó menor representación y heterogeneidad metodológica. Conclusión: La evidencia revela una carga multidimensional y heterogénea del HPV en mujeres adultas, con predominio de información epidemiológica y cervical, mientras que la dimensión económica y las localizaciones extracervicales permanecen menos estudiadas.

title: Efficiency of screening strategies to prevent cervical cancer in Eastern Africa
abstract: Cervical cancer (Cervix Uteri Carcinoma, CUC) is caused by an infection with the human papillomavirus (HPV), i.e., it involves both an infectious dimension (HPV infection) and the later development of a carcinoma as a chronic degenerative disease. Thus, it represents a rather unique case at the intersection of infectious and non-communicable diseases. A system dynamics model was developed to represent CUC disease progression and evaluate the economic determinants and cost-effectiveness of HPV self-sampling in Mozambique, Ethiopia, Uganda and Tanzania as model regions for Eastern African countries. The model was utilised to quantify and analyse the spread of the disease and depict the individual dynamics of the regions, and determined the factors which are most influential on the cost-effectiveness of a combined VIA and self-sampling scheme. The core finding of this simulation is that the integration of a HPV self-sampling scheme into an existing VIA regimen improves health outcomes by reducing the CUC burden, and will be cost-effective for the Eastern African countries (while not under all circumstances highly cost-effective), though it acts as a complementary tool rather than an automatic cost-saving panacea.

title: Gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma with peritoneal dissemination after chemoradiotherapy: a case report and review of the literature
abstract: Background Gastric-type endocervical adenocarcinoma (GAS) is the most common HPV-independent cervical adenocarcinoma. It is characterized by diagnostic difficulty, resistance to chemoradiotherapy and a propensity for peritoneal spread. Case presentation A 68-year-old woman presented with chronic hypogastric pain and a large hydrometra. Cervical cytology and an initial biopsy were non-diagnostic. A repeat biopsy established GAS (CK7-positive; p16, CK20, CDX2, estrogen receptor and PAX8-negative; wild-type p53; negative high-risk HPV by PCR), FIGO 2018 stage IIB, with negative staging imaging. After concurrent cisplatin-based chemoradiotherapy and brachytherapy, MRI showed only a 23% reduction of the tumor. Radical hysterectomy, delayed by six months, revealed residual tumor with omental and pelvic peritoneal metastases that had not been detected on staging imaging. She received five cycles of carboplatin–paclitaxel as first-line systemic therapy, complicated by grade 3 radiation proctitis, right ureteral and vesicovaginal fistulas, and severe hematologic toxicity. Eight months after completing chemotherapy, she developed malignant bowel obstruction from peritoneal progression. PD-L1 was negative (combined positive score 0). She died under palliative care 25 months after diagnosis. Conclusions This case illustrates the diagnostic pitfalls and radioresistance of GAS and its capacity for peritoneal spread. Together with a focused review of published locally advanced cases, it suggests that staging laparoscopy and earlier comprehensive biomarker testing deserve prospective evaluation.

title: Improving Knowledge of Reproductive Health and Preventing Risky Sexual Behavior as an Effort to Prevent Cervical Cancer Among Senior High School Students
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major public health problem in Indonesia, largely due to limited reproductive health literacy, inadequate awareness of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) infection, and insufficient preventive behaviors among adolescents. School-based reproductive health education is considered an important strategy for improving knowledge and promoting healthy behaviors before adulthood. This community service program aimed to improve students' knowledge of reproductive health, prevention of risky sexual behavior, and cervical cancer prevention through interactive health education and participatory turmeric antiseptic soap-making activities. The program was conducted on 16–17 April 2026 at SMA Negeri 1 Tawangsari Sukoharjo, involving 133 senior high school students. The intervention adopted a participatory community empowerment approach consisting of interactive lectures, group discussions, demonstrations, and hands-on production of turmeric antiseptic soap. Program effectiveness was evaluated using pre-test and post-test questionnaires. Descriptive statistics and paired-samples t-test were used to analyze changes in participants' knowledge. Participants' mean knowledge scores increased from 67.15 ± 19.34 before the intervention to 85.60 ± 18.22 after the intervention. The proportion of participants with good knowledge increased from 44.4% to 78.9%, while the poor knowledge category decreased from 18.8% to 8.3%. Paired-samples t-test analysis demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in knowledge following the intervention (t = −7.004; p < 0.001). Integrating reproductive health education with participatory practical activities effectively improved adolescents' knowledge regarding reproductive health and cervical cancer prevention. This educational model has the potential to be implemented sustainably through school health programs and replicated in other secondary schools to strengthen adolescent reproductive health promotion.

title: The Contribution of a Health Society to Immunization in Saudi Arabia: a Community Case study of the Waey Association for Community Health
abstract: Background: Non-Profit Organizations (NPOs) are long-standing partners in immunization, yet documented examples from state-led health systems remain scarce. This case study examines how a Saudi health society contributes to immunization through a surge workforce and vaccine demand beyond childhood. Methods: A community case study was conducted through document analysis of the program documentation of the Waey Association for Community Health, compiled for the 8th Saudi International Vaccination Forum (Riyadh, 2026). Activity domains were profiled against an explicit inclusion rule, reported outputs were converted into derived indicators, and each domain was coded against seven NPO roles drawn from a global scoping review; the findings were then synthesized into an explanatory model. Results: Six immunization domains addressing coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), human papillomavirus (HPV), seasonal influenza, and adult vaccination were identified, alongside two supporting activities. Deployment to COVID-19 vaccination centers mobilized 313 volunteers for 24,778 hours (79.2 hours per volunteer); the 2024 to 2025 community vaccination program mobilized 336 volunteers for 9,628 hours and reached 14,281 beneficiaries through 17 activities. The COVID-19 deployment thus supplied 72.0% of combined hours from 48.2% of volunteers. Four of seven NPO roles were represented, led by service delivery and demand generation. Conclusions: The society functioned as a reservoir of trained surge capacity and as a channel for vaccine demand among adolescents and adults. Both functions drew on shared assets, and a minimum reporting standard covering doses, unique beneficiaries, volunteer hours, and population denominators would allow them to be evaluated.

title: Giant Condyloma Acuminata pada Pasien dengan HIV: Laporan Kasus dengan Follow-Up Satu Tahun Setelah Eksisi dengan Elektrodesikasi
abstract: Giant condyloma acuminata (GCA) atau Buschke–Löwenstein tumor (BLT) merupakan lesi verukosa jarang dengan sifat klinis agresif, berkaitan erat dengan infeksi human papillomavirus (HPV) tipe 6 dan 11, serta memiliki potensi invasi lokal dan kekambuhan yang tinggi, terutama pada pasien imunokompromi (HIV). Kasus: Laki-laki usia 23 tahun dengan HIV yang sedang menjalani terapi antiretroviral (ARV) dan berperilaku seksual berisiko, dengan keluhan massa verukosa multipel menyerupai jengger ayam di regio anogenital dan perianal sejak sekitar tiga tahun. Pasien dilakukan eksisi menggunakan bedah listrik, terapi suportif, dan melanjutkan terapi antiretroviral. Selama pemantauan satu tahun pascatindakan, tidak ditemukan kekambuhan. Diskusi: GCA merupakan pertumbuhan lanjut dari kondiloma akuminata (KA) dengan karakteristik klinis agresif, meskipun secara histopatologis bersifat jinak. Eksisi bedah luas menjadi terapi pilihan, sedangkan terapi non-bedah dan imunoterapi dapat digunakan pada kasus tertentu. Keberhasilan terapi dipengaruhi oleh eksisi adekuat, perbaikan status imun, dan pengendalian faktor risiko. Pencegahan, contoh vaksinasi HPV, penting untuk mencegah infeksi tipe lain dan menurunkan kejadian lesi baru. GCA pada pasien imunokompromi (HIV) memerlukan penatalaksanaan komprehensif dengan eksisi bedah luas dan peningkatan status imun. Pemantauan berkelanjutan penting untuk mendeteksi kekambuhan secara dini.

title: Prevalence of Human Herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) in breast and colorectal cancer tissues compared with normal tissues in Shiraz, Iran
abstract: Human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) is associated with endothelial and B-cell malignancies; however, its potential involvement in epithelial cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, remains controversial. Therefore, in this study, we aimed to investigate the prevalence of HHV-8 DNA in malignant tissues of colorectal and breast cancers compared with non-malignant tissues in Shiraz, Iran. In this study, 210 specimens of colorectal paraffin-embedded tissue, including 70 normal mucosa, 70 adenomatous polyps, and 70 adenocarcin​omas, as well as 287 paraffin-embedded breast specimens, including 144 malignant and 143 benign lesions, were included. After deparafinization, the DNA was extracted using a commercial kit. The quality of the extracted DNA was evaluated using PCR on the beta globin gene. Those samples that were positive for the beta globin gene were screened for HHV-8 DNA using real-time PCR. χ2, or Fisher’s exact tests were used for statistical analysis. The mean age of colorectal patients was 52 ± 1.64 years, while the mean age was 45.0 ± 9.4 years in the malignant breast cancer group and 35.2 ± 12.1 years in the benign breast lesion group. In colorectal cancer, 112 cases (53.3%) were men. HHV-8 DNA was detected in 36/210 (17.1%) of colorectal samples, including 13/70 (18.6%) of normal mucosa, 12/70 (17.1%) of adenomas, and 11/70(15.7%) of adenocarcinomas, with no significant differences among groups ( p = 0.942). HHV-8 detection in colorectal tissues was not associated with sex, age strata, anatomic sub-site, or HPV co-infection (all p > 0.05). Moreover, the results of qPCR showed that in the breast tissues, HHV-8 DNA was identified in 31/144 (21.5%) malignant specimens and 28/143 (19.6%) benign specimens, which was not significantly different between the two groups ( p = 0.770). HHV-8 DNA was detected at low and comparable frequencies in normal, premalignant, and malignant colorectal tissues as well as in malignant versus benign breast specimens, providing no evidence for tumor-specific enrichment. These findings support an incidental/background carriage model rather than a direct oncogenic role in these epithelial cancers; tissue-localization and viral-load studies are warranted.

title: Lesão oral com aspectos histopatológicos sugestivos de condiloma acuminado em paciente indígena: relato de experiência.
abstract: This study reports the dental care of an 18-year-old Indigenous male patient presenting with an approximately 4-mm nodular lesion on the lower lip. The lesion had been present for about two months, with a history of itching, bleeding, and local trauma. Traumatic fibroma was the initial clinical hypothesis, and an excisional biopsy was performed on November 26, 2025. Histopathological examination of two specimens from the same clinical lesion showed chronic ulcerated inflammation with reactive hyperplasia in one specimen and acanthosis, parakeratosis, early papillomatosis, and koilocytosis in the other, leading to a report of morphological features suggestive of condyloma acuminatum, with no signs of malignancy. No molecular tests were performed to confirm human papillomavirus infection or determine a viral genotype. After the pathology report, the patient was referred to the local Multidisciplinary Indigenous Health Team for continued follow-up. This case highlights the importance of clinicopathological correlation in the differential diagnosis of oral lesions and of continuity of care through a culturally respectful approach.

title: Targeted antagonism of the Activator Protein 1 transcription factor complex results in potent anti-tumor activity in HNSCC and NSCLC models
abstract: The activator protein 1 (AP-1) transcription factor complex, comprised of Jun, Fos, ATF and Maf family members, is a critical driver of tumor pathogenesis and metastasis and represents an attractive but traditionally challenging therapeutic target. The Fos family member Fra-1, whose elevated expression correlates with poor prognosis in human papilloma virus-negative (HPV-) head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), promotes oncogenic pathways including proliferation, survival, and invasion. As dimerization is required for AP-1 complex DNA binding and transcriptional activity, we designed a Fra-1-antagonist peptide, ST712, as a therapeutic candidate to disrupt complex formation and prevent associated activity. Antagonism of the Fra-1 and c-Jun protein-protein interaction with ST712 attenuated AP-1 transcriptional activity and significantly impacted invasion, apoptosis and proliferation pathways. Following exposure to ST712, a phenotypic mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition was observed that prevented in vitro invasion. Additionally, ST712 exposure led to dose-dependent induction of apoptosis and G1 arrest. Consistent with its impact on cell cycle, combination of ST712 with the CDK4/6 inhibitor abemaciclib resulted in synergistic anti-tumor activity in vitro. Further, while ST712 monotherapy resulted in significant anti-tumor activity in HNSCC and NSCLC subcutaneous xenograft models, combination of sub-pharmacologic ST712 and abemaciclib resulted in significantly enhanced tumor growth inhibition in HNSCC models. These data support ST712 as a potent peptide antagonist of the AP-1 transcription factor that warrants further development as a novel therapeutic option for AP-1 driven tumors such as HPV- HNSCC and NSCLC.

title: Machine learning-assisted SERS-based profiling of blood serum filtrate fractions in cervical cancer using 50 kDa filtration devices
abstract: Persistent infection with human papillomavirus (HPV) (HPV-16 and HPV-18) is the main cause of cervical cancer, and it continues to be one of the common causes of cancer-related deaths in women globally. To detect this cancer at an early stage, several diagnostic methods have been explored, but still a need for an easy-to-perform, non-destructive, and non-invasive method that can detect this cancer with high sensitivity in a short time. In this study, SERS was used to detect and classify cervical cancer using blood serum filtrate fractions collected with 50 kDa ultrafiltration devices. In filtrate fractions, prominent SERS spectral peaks were recorded at 326, 345, 883, 927, 1102, 1133, 1203, and 1403 cm-1 which could be used as potential cervical cancer biomarkers. As a SERS substrate, silver nanoparticles (Ag-NPs) were used to enhance spectral resolution and the intensity of weak Raman signals. SERS spectra of serum samples from cervical cancer and healthy patients were analyzed by principal component analysis. The four-class PLS-DA model was subsequently developed using sample-level partitioning to distinguish healthy controls from stage 2, stage 3, and stage 4 cervical cancer samples. Sample-level LOOCV identified eight latent variables as the optimal model complexity, with a maximum LOOCV accuracy of 81.82%. Independent sample-level validation yielded an overall classification accuracy of 86.67%, while one-versus-rest AUC values were 1.000, 0.909, 0.955, and 1.000 for healthy, stage 2, stage 3, and stage 4, respectively.

title: Optimising risk stratification for atypical glandular cells: insights from a large Chinese gynaecologic cohort
abstract: Aims To optimise risk-stratified management of atypical glandular cells (AGC) by evaluating risk factors for cervical and endometrial pathology. Methods We retrospectively analysed 2460 AGC patients without prior malignancy (2007–2024), examining AGC subtypes, age, high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) genotypes, ultrasound findings and histological outcomes. Results Atypical endometrial cells (AEM) predicted endometrial lesions (30.3%, 95% CI 25.9% to 35.1%) versus other subtypes (5.4%, 95% CI 4.2% to 6.9%, p<0.001). AGC endocervical cells, favour neoplastic (AEC-FN), and AGC, favour neoplastic (AGC-FN) had higher significant lesion risks than non-neoplastic AGC (69.8%, 95% CI 62.9% to 75.9% vs 21.4%, 95% CI 19.2% to 23.8%, p<0.001). Age ≥45 plus positive ultrasound improved endometrial prediction (AUC 0.825 vs 0.732, p<0.001). HPV18 and HPV16 conferred highest cervical risks (68.8%, 95% CI 58.3% to 77.8% and 50.3%, 95% CI 42.3% to 58.3%), with HPV18 linked to cervical glandular lesions (58.1%, 95% CI 47.4% to 68.2%). hrHPV-negative patients with significant lesions predominantly had endometrial pathology (69.2%, 95% CI 61.6% to 76.0%). Conclusions AGC subtyping provides clinically meaningful risk stratification: AEM indicates endometrial evaluation; AEC-FN and AGC-FN indicate cervical evaluation. Age and ultrasound may refine endometrial risk assessment. HPV genotyping guides cervical evaluation but endometrial assessment remains important in hrHPV-negative patients. These findings suggest a potential approach requiring prospective validation before clinical application.

title: Recidiva de Lesões Intraepiteliais Cervicais Após Conização Por Cirurgia de Alta Frequência (CAF): Revisão Integrativa da Literatura
abstract: Introdução: As lesões intraepiteliais cervicais representam alterações precursoras do câncer do colo uterino, sendo frequentemente associadas à infecção persistente pelo HPV. Embora a conização por cirurgia de alta frequência (CAF) seja uma abordagem eficaz para o tratamento das lesões de alto grau, a persistência ou recorrência das alterações permanece um desafio clínico. Objetivo: Realizar uma revisão integrativa da literatura sobre a recidiva de lesões intraepiteliais cervicais após conização por CAF, identificando sua frequência, fatores de risco e estratégias de acompanhamento e prevenção. Método: Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa realizada na base de dados PubMed, utilizando a estratégia: (("recurrence"[ti] OR "recurrent"[ti] OR "residual disease"[ti] OR "persistent disease"[ti]) AND ("cervical intraepithelial neoplasia"[ti] OR "cervical intraepithelial lesion"[ti] OR "squamous intraepithelial lesion"[ti] OR CIN[ti] OR HSIL[ti] OR LSIL[ti]) AND ("conization"[ti] OR "cone biopsy"[ti] OR LEEP[ti] OR LLETZ[ti] OR "loop electrosurgical excision procedure"[ti] OR "large loop excision of the transformation zone"[ti]). Foram considerados estudos publicados no último ano. Resultados: Foram identificados dez artigos, dos quais dois foram excluídos, sendo um por se tratar de errata e outro de nota editorial, totalizando oito estudos incluídos. Os resultados apontaram o comprometimento das margens cirúrgicas e a persistência do HPV de alto risco como principais fatores associados à recorrência. Imunossupressão, tabagismo, lesões de maior grau e comprometimento glandular também foram relacionados ao aumento do risco. A vacinação contra o HPV apresentou resultados promissores na prevenção de novas lesões. Conclusão: A identificação dos fatores prognósticos e o acompanhamento pós-operatório individualizado são fundamentais para detectar precocemente as recidivas e aprimorar a prevenção do câncer cervical.

title: Factors associated with HPV vaccination among female college students in China: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is central to cervical cancer elimination. Before China introduced free bivalent HPV vaccination for eligible 13-year-old girls through the national immunisation programme in November 2025, uptake among young women was shaped by out-of-pocket payment, regional service access, and socioeconomic position. This study estimated pre-implementation uptake and examined individual and structural factors associated with vaccination among female college students in China. Data came from the 2025 National College Students’ Sexual and Reproductive Health Survey (NCSS-SRH). The analytic sample comprised 44,052 female respondents with valid HPV vaccination responses. Vaccinated respondents reported at least one dose of bivalent, quadrivalent, or 9-valent vaccine. Weighted multivariable logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for reproductive health knowledge, sexuality education, gender temperament, penetrative sexual intercourse, age, grade, residence, region, monthly expenditure, and school type. Weighted HPV vaccination uptake was 18.4%. Among vaccinated students, 74.9% reported receiving 9-valent vaccine. Uptake increased from 11.6% in the lowest reproductive health knowledge quartile to 24.5% in the highest. In the adjusted model, knowledge was positively associated with vaccination (aOR 2.19, 95% CI 1.97–2.45). Positive associations were also observed for school-based sexuality education (aOR 1.17, 95% CI 1.09–1.26), penetrative sexual intercourse (aOR 1.20, 95% CI 1.11–1.30), urban residence (aOR 1.65, 95% CI 1.56–1.73), monthly expenditure of at least CNY 2000 versus less than CNY 1000 (aOR 2.13, 95% CI 1.95–2.32), undergraduate study (aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.34–1.50), and postgraduate study (aOR 4.07, 95% CI 3.54–4.67). Compared with Eastern China, adjusted odds were lower in Central (aOR 0.39, 95% CI 0.37–0.42) and Western China (aOR 0.86, 95% CI 0.81–0.91). HPV vaccination uptake among female college students was low before national programme implementation and was socially and geographically patterned. Catch-up strategies for college-age women should combine reproductive health education with financing and delivery measures that reduce access barriers, with particular attention to lower-expenditure students, junior college students, non-urban residents, and institutions in regions with low uptake.

title: Triplet tumbling microscopy enables in situ quantification of protein complex assembly and dynamics
abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) mediate diverse cellular processes but are typically characterized in vitro with recombinant proteins. Current cell-compatible approaches for measuring PPIs have limited scope and often require prior knowledge of the interacting partners. Here, we develop triplet tumbling microscopy (TTM) to reveal PPIs in cells in real time. TTM reports protein complex size from rotational diffusion ("tumbling") by leveraging infrared-triggerable emission from triplet states. These long-lived triplets overcome the size limitations of traditional fluorescence anisotropy, enabling TTM to measure species from small protein complexes to organelle-scale beads. We apply TTM to detect PPIs, quantify bound fractions, and distinguish protein complexes by size. We measure diverse interactions, including rapamycin-induced dimerization, p53 homo-oligomerization, and binding of the E3-ligase E6AP to the human papilloma virus 16 E6 protein. TTM hardware is compatible with most fluorescence microscopes, providing a versatile way to access molecular insights within cells.

title_original: HPV16 E6 promotes the proliferation of cervical cancer cells through the CPT1A/c-Myc positive feedback loop.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the mechanism by which HPV16 E6 promotes the proliferation of cervical cancer cells, addressing a gap in understanding the molecular pathways involved in HPV-associated carcinogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in vitro using cervical cancer cell lines, focusing on the role of HPV16 E6 in cellular proliferation without involving human or animal populations.
analysis.methods: The researchers used molecular biology techniques, including gene expression analysis and cell proliferation assays, to examine the interaction between HPV16 E6 and the CPT1A/c-Myc pathway.
analysis.main_results: The study found that HPV16 E6 significantly promotes cervical cancer cell proliferation through a positive feedback loop involving CPT1A and c-Myc, with specific molecular interactions observed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted their findings as evidence of a novel regulatory mechanism by which HPV16 E6 enhances cancer cell growth, highlighting the importance of the CPT1A/c-Myc axis in this process.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings contribute to the understanding of HPV16's role in cervical cancer progression, potentially informing targeted therapeutic strategies for HPV-associated malignancies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro models, which may not fully represent in vivo conditions, and the evidence is based on a single cell line, reducing generalizability. The confidence in these findings is moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how HPV16 E6 promotes cervical cancer cell proliferation through a positive feedback loop involving CPT1A and c-Myc. The research was conducted in vitro using cervical cancer cell lines, employing molecular biology techniques to analyze gene expression and cell growth. The main results demonstrate a significant enhancement of cell proliferation linked to the CPT1A/c-Myc pathway, suggesting a novel mechanism in HPV-associated carcinogenesis. The authors interpret these findings as highlighting the importance of this pathway in HPV16's oncogenic effects, which could inform future therapeutic strategies. However, the study's reliance on in vitro models limits its applicability to real-world scenarios, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength due to the limited scope of the experimental setup.

full_text: Abstract Purpose Human papillomavirus (HPV)-positive and HPV-negative oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) are biologically distinct entities with different clinical behaviors and therapeutic responses. However, genomic studies of OPSCC have largely focused on Western populations, and the molecular landscape in Asian patients remains incompletely defined. This study characterized genomic alterations, mutational signatures, and therapeutic actionability of OPSCC according to HPV status in an Asian cohort. Methods This multicenter tissue-based next-generation sequencing registry study (TCOG T1322; NCT05522881, registered on August 31, 2022) enrolled patients with pathologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan. Tumor samples underwent comprehensive genomic profiling using a 440-gene targeted panel. Tumor genomic alterations, pathway dysregulation, mutational signatures, tumor mutational burden (TMB), and therapeutic actionability were analyzed by p16-defined HPV status. Results Among 290 patients with OPSCC, 190 had HPV-positive and 100 had HPV-negative tumors. HPV-positive OPSCC frequently harbored alterations in PIK3CA (37%), BCL6 (14%), and immune checkpoint ligand amplifications CD274/PDCD1LG2 (6%). HPV-negative tumors were enriched for TP53 mutations (89%), CDKN2A deletions (34%), FAT1 alterations (33%), and CCND1 amplifications (30%). HPV-negative tumors showed greater dysregulation of cell cycle, differentiation, and oxidative stress pathways, whereas HPV-positive tumors were enriched for immune-related alterations. APOBEC-associated single-base-substitution (SBS) signatures SBS2/SBS13 predominated in HPV-positive tumors, while SBS5/SBS16 were more common in HPV-negative tumors. Among HPV-positive tumors, smokers demonstrated higher BCL6 and TP53 alterations and distinct mutational patterns. HPV-positive tumors also had higher TMB and greater prevalence of TMB-high status. Conclusions OPSCC exhibits distinct p16-defined genomic profiles in this Asian cohort, providing insights into its biological heterogeneity and identifying potential translational therapeutic targets for further investigation. Methods This multicenter tissue-based next-generation sequencing registry study (TCOG T1322; NCT05522881, registered on August 31, 2022) enrolled patients with pathologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan. analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genomic profiles of oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma (OPSCC) in an Asian cohort, distinguishing between HPV-positive and HPV-negative tumors. It enrolled 290 patients with pathologically confirmed head and neck squamous cell carcinoma in Taiwan, using a 440-gene targeted panel for comprehensive genomic profiling. Results showed that HPV-positive tumors had frequent alterations in PIK3CA, BCL6, and immune checkpoint ligands, while HPV-negative tumors were enriched for TP53 mutations, CDKN2A deletions, FAT1 alterations, and CCND1 amplifications. The findings suggest distinct biological features of HPV-positive and HPV-negative OPSCC in this population, offering potential insights for targeted therapies. However, the study's focus on an Asian cohort may limit its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the specific context and lack of broader validation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在调查亚洲人 队列研究 口咽鳞状细胞癌 (OPSCC) 的基因组谱,因为 HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性 OPSCC 是生物学上不同的实体,具有不同的临床行为和治疗反应。这项研究是必要的,因为 OPSCC 的基因组研究主要集中在西方人群,而亚洲患者的分子格局尚未完全确定。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项在台湾进行的多中心基于组织的下一代测序注册研究(TCOG T1322;NCT05522881),招募了经病理证实的头颈鳞状细胞癌患者。该研究纳入了 290 名 OPSCC 患者,其中 190 名患有 HPV 阳性肿瘤,100 名患有 HPV 阴性肿瘤。
elements_zh.methods: 使用 440 个基因靶向组对肿瘤样本进行全面的基因组分析。根据 p16 定义的 HPV 状态分析基因组改变、通路失调、突变特征、肿瘤突变负荷 (TMB) 和治疗可操作性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 290 名 OPSCC 患者中,190 名患有 HPV 阳性肿瘤,100 名患有 HPV 阴性肿瘤。HPV 阳性肿瘤经常存在 PIK3CA (37%)、BCL6 (14%) 和免疫检查点配体扩增 CD274/PDCD1LG2 (6%) 的改变。HPV 阴性肿瘤富含 TP53 突变 (89%)、CDKN2A 缺失 (34%)、FAT1 改变 (33%) 和 CCND1 扩增 (30%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现强调了亚洲 队列研究 中 HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性 OPSCC 的不同基因组图谱,为了解其生物异质性提供了见解,并确定了潜在的转化治疗靶点以供进一步研究。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果有助于了解亚洲人群中 HPV 阳性和 HPV 阴性 OPSCC 之间的分子差异,这可能为该特定人群提供更有针对性的诊断和治疗策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其对亚洲 队列研究 的关注而受到限制,这可能会影响研究结果对其他人群的普遍适用性。证据是中等的,因为它基于特定 队列研究 的基因组分析,未经更广泛的验证。
